body: LegalSpain · LegalRefund PolicyVersion 2 · Last updated 18 July 2026All legal documentsDownload PDFRefund Policy All Markets | Consultations, Credits, Physical Products, Home Delivery Effective Date: 1 July 2026 Refund Policy — Summary OperatorGlobal Guest s.r.o. trading as Global Health IČO19071680 Contactglobalhealth@myglobalhealth.online MarketsSee www.myglobalhealth.online/markets Refund contactglobalhealth@myglobalhealth.online — subject: "Refund Request" Refund processing timeWithin 14 days of approval (EU) / 7 business days (Brazil) Effective Date1 July 2026 Quick Reference — Refund Scenarios The table below summarises the refund outcome for each scenario. Full details for each category are set out in the sections that follow. ScenarioOutcomeMarkets Consultation cancelled ≥24h beforeCredits reinstated in fullAll markets Consultation cancelled <24h beforeCredits forfeitedAll markets Consultation cancelled <24h — medical emergencyCredits reinstated (with documentation)All markets Consultation not delivered — platform faultCredits reinstated + cash refund optionAll markets No-showCredits forfeitedAll markets Credit Plan — within 14-day cooling-off, no credits usedFull cash refundEU markets Credit Plan — within 14-day cooling-off, credits usedPro-rata cash refundEU markets Credit Plan — within 7-day cooling-off, no credits usedFull cash refundBrazil Credit Plan — after cooling-off, unused creditsNon-refundableAll markets One-off credits — unusedNon-refundableAll markets Home Health Test Kit — unopened, within 14 daysFull refundAll markets Home Health Test Kit — opened or after 14 daysNon-refundableAll markets Home Health Test Kit — damaged on arrivalFull refund or replacementAll markets Telemedicine Device — unused, within 30 daysFull refundAll markets Telemedicine Device — used or after 30 daysNon-refundableAll markets Telemedicine Device — defective on arrivalFull refund or replacementAll markets Home Delivery — before dispatchFull refundIreland only Home Delivery — after dispatchNon-refundableIreland only 1. Introduction This Refund Policy applies to all products and services purchased through the Global Health platform at www.myglobalhealth.online, operated by Global Guest s.r.o. (IČO: 19071680) trading as Global Health. Global Health offers four categories of purchasable items, each with its own refund rules: (1) medical consultations booked individually or using Credits; (2) Credit Plans (monthly subscriptions); (3) physical products including Home Health Test Kits and Telemedicine Devices; and (4) Home Delivery services (Ireland only). Your statutory consumer rights in your country of residence are not affected by this Policy and take precedence where they provide greater protection. The statutory rights applicable in your market are set out in the Country Addendum for your market, available at www.myglobalhealth.online/terms. To request a refund, email globalhealth@myglobalhealth.online with the subject line "Refund Request". Include your full name, account email address, booking or order reference, and the reason for your request. We will acknowledge your request within 2 business days. 2. Medical Consultations 2.1 Cancellation more than 24 hours before the appointment If you cancel a confirmed consultation at least 24 hours before the scheduled appointment time, any Credits used to book the consultation will be reinstated to your account in full. If you paid by direct payment (not Credits), you will receive a full refund to your original payment method within 14 days. 2.2 Cancellation less than 24 hours before the appointment If you cancel a confirmed consultation less than 24 hours before the scheduled appointment time, the Credits or payment used to book the consultation are forfeited. No refund or Credit reinstatement will be issued, except in the circumstances set out in clause 2.3. 2.3 Exceptions to the late cancellation rule Credits or payment will be reinstated or refunded where the late cancellation is due to: A documented medical emergency affecting you or an immediate family member — we may request supporting documentation at our discretion. A platform-side failure that prevented you from accessing or completing the consultation — in this case reinstatement is automatic. The Clinician cancelling or failing to attend the consultation — see clause 2.5. 2.4 Rescheduling You may reschedule a confirmed consultation up to 12 hours before the scheduled appointment time without incurring any Credit charge or fee. Each booking may be rescheduled once without charge. Further rescheduling requests will be treated as a cancellation under clause 2.2. 2.5 Consultation not delivered — platform or Clinician fault If a booked consultation cannot proceed within 2 hours of the scheduled time due to a reason attributable to Global Health or the Clinician, you will be offered: Full reinstatement of any Credits used, credited to your account immediately; or A full cash refund of the monetary value of the Credits or payment used, processed to your original payment method within 14 days. You may choose either option. Please contact globalhealth@myglobalhealth.online to request your preferred remedy. 2.6 No-show If you fail to attend a scheduled consultation without prior cancellation or rescheduling notice, the Credits or payment used to book that consultation are forfeited. No reinstatement or refund will be issued. 2.7 Quality concerns If you have concerns about the quality of a consultation, please refer to our complaints procedure at www.myglobalhealth.online/complaints. Quality concerns are handled through our clinical governance process and are not processed as refund requests. Your statutory rights as a consumer in your jurisdiction are not affected by this clause. 3. Credits and Credit Plans 3.1 What are Credits? Credits are the unit of value used to book Services on the Platform. Credits may be obtained by subscribing to a monthly Credit Plan or by purchasing them on a one-off basis. Credits have no cash value and are non-transferable between accounts. 3.2 Statutory cooling-off period — Credit Plan subscriptions Your statutory cooling-off rights depend on your country of residence: EU markets (Ireland, Portugal, Czech Republic, Spain, Romania): You have a 14-day right of withdrawal from the date of first subscription. If you cancel within 14 days and have not used any Credits, you will receive a full cash refund of the subscription fee to your original payment method within 14 days. If you have used Credits during the cooling-off period, a proportionate deduction reflecting the monetary value of Credits used will apply. Brazil: You have a 7-day right of withdrawal from the date of first subscription under Artigo 49 of the Código de Defesa do Consumidor. If you cancel within 7 days and have not used any Credits, you will receive a full cash refund within 7 business days. If Credits have been used, a proportionate deduction applies. 3.3 Credits used — non-refundable Credits that have been used to book a consultation or service are non-refundable, subject to the cancellation and consultation fault provisions in Section 2. 3.4 Unused Credits after cooling-off period — non-refundable Credits that remain unused in your account after the statutory cooling-off period has expired are non-refundable. This applies to both Credit Plan Credits and one-off Credits purchased outside a Plan. 3.5 Credit Plan cancellation — no refund for unused portion of current billing cycle When you cancel a Credit Plan, cancellation takes effect at the end of the current monthly billing cycle. You retain access to all Credits and Plan benefits until the end of the paid period. No partial refund is issued for any unused portion of the current billing cycle after the cooling-off period has expired. 3.6 Carry-forward of unused Plan Credits after cancellation Credits allocated under a cancelled Credit Plan remain available in your account for 12 months from the cancellation date. After 12 months, unused Plan Credits expire and are not refundable. One-off Credits purchased outside a Plan are unaffected by Plan cancellation and do not expire. 3.7 Account closure If you close your Global Health account, any Credits remaining in your account are forfeited and are not refundable, unless you close your account in response to a material change to these Terms, in which case Credits will be refunded at their monetary value within 10 business days as set out in the Master Terms. 3.8 One-off Credits Credits purchased on a one-off basis outside of a Credit Plan are non-refundable once purchased, except as required by applicable consumer law in your jurisdiction. One-off Credits do not expire and carry forward indefinitely while your account is active. 4. Home Health Test Kits Home Health Test Kits are physical products dispatched to your address. The following refund policy applies to all test kits purchased through the Platform. 4.1 14-day return window — unopened kits You may return a Home Health Test Kit within 14 days of delivery and receive a full refund, provided the kit is: Completely unopened and in its original sealed packaging. Unused and unactivated — including any digital activation codes or registration steps. Returned with all original components, instructions, and packaging included. Return shipping costs are your responsibility unless the return is due to a defect or incorrect item received. 4.2 Opened or activated kits — non-refundable Due to health, hygiene, and safety regulations, we cannot accept returns of Home Health Test Kits that have been opened, activated, or used in any way. This applies even if the test has not been completed or the results have not been processed. No refund will be issued for opened or activated kits. 4.3 Damaged, defective, or incorrect items If your kit arrives damaged, defective, or is not what you ordered, please contact us at globalhealth@myglobalhealth.online within 48 hours of delivery with photographs of the item and packaging. We will offer either: A full refund to your original payment method within 14 days; or A replacement kit dispatched at no additional charge. You choose your preferred remedy. We will cover return shipping costs for damaged, defective, or incorrect items. 4.4 How to initiate a return Email globalhealth@myglobalhealth.online with the subject line "Refund Request — Test Kit". Include your full name, order reference number, reason for return, and photographs if relevant. We will provide return instructions and a return address upon approval. Return shipping costs are your responsibility. Where a return involves shipping from outside Ireland, we will advise on the most cost-effective return method — if return shipping costs would be disproportionate, we may arrange an alternative remedy such as a replacement or credit. 5. Telemedicine Devices Telemedicine Devices are physical electronic items used in conjunction with the Global Health Platform. Examples include connected health monitoring devices, digital stethoscopes, and similar equipment. 5.1 30-day return window — unused devices You may return a Telemedicine Device within 30 days of delivery and receive a full refund, provided the device is: Unused and in its original condition with no signs of use or wear. In its original packaging with all accessories, cables, manuals, and protective materials included. Not registered, activated, or paired with any account or application. Return shipping costs are your responsibility unless the return is due to a defect or incorrect item. 5.2 Used devices — non-refundable Telemedicine Devices that show signs of use, have been activated or registered, or are returned after 30 days of delivery are not eligible for a refund. 5.3 Defective or incorrect devices If a device arrives defective, damaged, or is not what you ordered, please contact us at globalhealth@myglobalhealth.online within 48 hours of delivery with photographs. We will offer either a full refund or a replacement at no additional charge. We cover return shipping for defective or incorrect devices. 5.4 Warranty Telemedicine Devices are covered by the manufacturer's warranty. Warranty terms vary by device and manufacturer and are included in the product documentation. Warranty claims after the 30-day return window should be directed to the manufacturer. Global Health will assist in facilitating warranty claims where possible. 6. Home Delivery — Ireland Only Ireland only: Home Delivery services are currently available in Ireland only. Home Delivery refers to the delivery of prescription medications or health products to your address in Ireland, facilitated by Global Health in conjunction with a registered pharmacy partner. 6.1 Cancellation before dispatch If you cancel a Home Delivery order before it has been dispatched from the pharmacy, you will receive a full refund to your original payment method within 14 days. To cancel before dispatch, contact globalhealth@myglobalhealth.online as soon as possible after placing the order. 6.2 Cancellation after dispatch — non-refundable Once a Home Delivery order has been dispatched from the pharmacy, it cannot be cancelled or returned due to the nature of prescription medications and applicable Irish medicines regulations. No refund will be issued after dispatch. 6.3 Non-delivery or incorrect delivery If your order is not delivered within the expected timeframe, or if the incorrect item is delivered, please contact globalhealth@myglobalhealth.online within 48 hours. We will investigate and, where applicable, arrange a replacement delivery or a full refund. 6.4 Damaged items on delivery If items arrive damaged, please photograph the items and packaging and contact us within 48 hours of delivery. We will arrange a replacement at no additional charge. 7. Your Statutory Consumer Rights This Refund Policy sets out Global Health's standard refund terms. schemaFaqs.question: What is an online specialist consultation?
schemaFaqs.answer: An online specialist consultation is an in-depth video review of your condition by a clinician registered with Organización Médica Colegial (colegios de médicos) who works in a specific medical area. The specialist reviews your history, symptoms and any existing investigations before advising on next steps.

schemaFaqs.question: How much does it cost?
schemaFaqs.answer: Online specialist consultations at Global Health cost from €70.00. There are no hidden fees and no membership required.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need a referral?
schemaFaqs.answer: A referral is not always required to book, but some specialties may request your GP notes or existing investigation results ahead of the appointment so the specialist can review your case fully.

schemaFaqs.question: Are online specialist consultations valid?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Consultations are conducted by doctors registered with Organización Médica Colegial (colegios de médicos) using secure video to national telemedicine standards.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens after my consultation?
schemaFaqs.answer: Following your consultation the specialist will send clinical notes and follow-up guidance to your email. Further investigations or a referral will be arranged where clinically indicated.

schemaFaqs.question: Which languages are available?
schemaFaqs.answer: Consultations are available in multiple languages, subject to clinician availability. You can select a specialist by language when booking.

title: Hair Loss Consultation Online Spain | Medical Assessment | Same Day
description: Losing hair or noticing thinning in Spain? Our OMC-registered GPs assess the medical cause of hair loss and advise on evidence-based management. Video consultation, same-day appointments anywhere in Spain.
h1: Hair Loss Consultation — Medical Assessment Online, Same Day in Spain
h2: Why Early Assessment Makes a Difference
Why Hair Loss Is Dismissed Too Often
Book Hair Loss Consultation in Spain

schemaFaqs.question: Can hair loss really be assessed by video call?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — for the vast majority of presentations. A detailed medical history is the most powerful diagnostic tool in the evaluation of hair loss, and a complete history can be taken by video call. Your doctor also asks you to show the affected areas during the call. Where physical examination findings or scalp biopsy are needed, your doctor advises you on appropriate referral.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need blood tests before my appointment?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Your doctor evaluates during the consultation whether the tests are indicated and requests the lab work the same day if so. Bring any recent results you have — your doctor reviews them in full.

schemaFaqs.question: Can hair loss be reversed?
schemaFaqs.answer: It depends on the type and how long it has been progressing. Androgenic alopecia responds better to treatment started early, when the follicles are thinning rather than already lost. Telogen effluvium is generally self-limited and resolves once the underlying cause is treated. Hair loss related to nutritional deficiency responds well to correcting the deficiency. Scarring alopecia requires urgent specialist evaluation because it can cause permanent loss if not treated.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service suitable for women with hair loss?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Female hair loss is a central part of this service. The clinical picture in women is often more complex than male androgenetic alopecia— involving hormonal, nutritional, and autoimmune factors — and benefits significantly from a structured clinical evaluation.

schemaFaqs.question: What if my hair loss is related to a medication I am taking?
schemaFaqs.answer: Hair loss related to medications is evaluated as part of this consultation. Your doctor reviews your current medication, identifies whether any may be contributing to your hair loss, and advises on appropriate management.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I get a referral to dermatology through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Where specialist dermatological assessment is clinically indicated, your primary care physician issues a referral letter the same day.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-payment service. The clinical documentation issued through this service is provided at the full private price regardless of insurance status.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera.

body: ++All consultationsOnline consultationHair Loss Consultation — Medical Assessment Online, Same Day in SpainHair loss is one of the most common medical concerns — and one of the most commonly dismissed. Most people who notice significant thinning or shedding never speak to a doctor about it, either because they assume nothing can be done, or because they do not know where to start. Both assumptions are wrong. In the vast majority of cases, hair loss has an identifiable medical cause — and the earlier it is assessed, the better the outcome. Hair follicles that have been inactive for a prolonged period are significantly harder to recover than follicles that are thinning but still active. Our GPs, registered with the Spanish Medical Council (OMC — Organización Médica Colegial), offer comprehensive hair loss assessments by secure video call — identifying the underlying cause, advising on evidence-based management, and issuing appropriate clinical documentation where clinically indicated. Same day, from anywhere in Spain, in English, Spanish, or Portuguese.Registered doctors · SpainSecure video consultationConfidential & GDPR-compliantClinically reviewed by Dra. María Fernanda Ocampo Mora· CGCOM | 291409735Book online€39per consultation15-minute appointmentDoctor registered in SpainInstant confirmation by emailConsultation summary includedBook this serviceSecure checkout · payments processed by StripeAbout this serviceWhy Early Assessment Makes a DifferenceHair loss almost always follows a progressive pattern — particularly androgenetic alopecia in both men and women. The clinical argument for early assessment is straightforward: the earlier the cause is identified and appropriate management initiated, the better the outcome. Waiting until hair loss is advanced significantly reduces the treatment options available.If you have noticed changes in your hair density, hairline, or shedding pattern — even if you are not sure whether it is significant enough to see a doctor about — book a consultation. Your doctor tells you honestly whether intervention is warranted and what the options are.Who This Service Is ForThis consultation is appropriate for adults experiencing:Gradual thinning of hair on the scalp — in men or womenReceding hairline or temporal thinningThinning at the crown or top of the scalpSudden or patchy hair lossDiffuse shedding — more hair in the shower, on the pillow, or in the brushHair loss following a significant life event — illness, surgery, childbirth, or intense stressHair loss associated with other symptoms — fatigue, weight changes, skin or nail changes — that may indicate an underlying conditionScalp health concerns — dandruff, seborrhoea, or inflammation affecting hair growthHair loss that has not responded to over-the-counter treatmentsConditions Commonly AssessedMale hair lossAndrogenetic alopecia — the most common cause of hair loss in men, assessed and managed at GP level including discussion of evidence-based treatment optionsAlopecia areata — patchy, autoimmune-basis hair lossTelogen effluvium — diffuse shedding following illness, stress, or nutritional deficiencySeborrhoeic dermatitis and scalp inflammation contributing to hair lossMedication-related hair loss — assessment and managementFemale hair lossFemale pattern androgenetic alopeciaTelogen effluvium — particularly post-partum, following significant illness, or after major stressAlopecia areataHair loss related to hormonal changes — PCOS, thyroid dysfunction, menopause, or post-partum hormonal changesHair loss related to nutritional deficiency — iron, ferritin, vitamin D, B12, and zincTraction alopecia — related to hairstyling practicesMedication-related hair lossBothTinea capitis — fungal scalp infection causing hair loss, requiring treatmentScarring alopecia — requires urgent dermatology referralHair loss as a symptom of systemic conditions — thyroid disease, autoimmune conditions, anaemiaWhat Your Consultation IncludesFull hair loss assessmentYour GP takes a detailed history of your hair loss — onset, pattern, rate of progression, family history, associated symptoms, current medications, nutritional status, recent life events, and general health — building a complete picture as the basis for identifying the cause.Identification of underlying causeHair loss is frequently a symptom of something systemic — not just an aesthetic concern. Your GP assesses hormonal, nutritional, autoimmune, and medication-related contributors that may be causing or accelerating your hair loss.Evidence-based management planBased on the assessment, your GP advises on the most appropriate approach for your specific type of hair loss — which may include nutritional optimisation, topical treatments, clinical recommendations at the doctor's professional discretion, and referral where indicated.Investigation requests where indicatedWhere blood tests are clinically indicated — thyroid function, ferritin, iron studies, hormonal panel, vitamin levels — your GP issues the request the same day.Clinical documentation — at the doctor's professional discretionWhen clinically indicated, your GP issues appropriate clinical documentation valid at any pharmacy in Spain.Note: Controlled substances cannot be issued electronically under Spanish law. Your doctor advises if this applies to your situation.Dermatology referral where neededCertain hair loss conditions — including scarring alopecia, complex alopecia areata, and presentations requiring scalp biopsy — require specialist dermatology assessment. Your GP advises clearly if this is your case and coordinates referral.Why Hair Loss Is Dismissed Too OftenHair loss is frequently met with "it is normal" or "it is just stress" — sometimes correctly, but too often without proper investigation. A GP who genuinely assesses hair loss does not start with a generic answer. They start with a complete history, assess the hormonal and nutritional picture, and identify the specific cause before proposing an approach tailored to that cause.The difference between "it is probably stress" without investigation and "your ferritin is low and this is causing telogen effluvium, which is treatable" with a blood test is not a small one. A detailed medical history is the most powerful diagnostic tool in the evaluation of hair loss, and a complete history can be taken by video call. Your doctor also asks you to show the affected areas during the call. Where physical examination findings or scalp biopsy are needed, your doctor advises you on appropriate referral.Do I need blood tests before my appointment?No. Your doctor evaluates during the consultation whether the tests are indicated and requests the lab work the same day if so. Bring any recent results you have — your doctor reviews them in full.Can hair loss be reversed?It depends on the type and how long it has been progressing. Androgenic alopecia responds better to treatment started early, when the follicles are thinning rather than already lost. Telogen effluvium is generally self-limited and resolves once the underlying cause is treated. Hair loss related to nutritional deficiency responds well to correcting the deficiency. schemaFaqs.question: Can the cardiologist interpret my ECG by video call?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — by sending the PDF or image of the ECG before the consultation. Your cardiologist interprets it in full before the call and explains the findings in detail during the consultation. This is an established practice in telecardiology.

schemaFaqs.question: I have symptoms of palpitations — is this urgent?
schemaFaqs.answer: Palpitations with dizziness, loss of consciousness, or chest pain are urgent — call 112 immediately. Palpitations without associated severe symptoms, especially if they are episodic and not worsening, are appropriate for non-urgent cardiology assessment through this service.

schemaFaqs.question: What tests should I bring to the consultation?
schemaFaqs.answer: Everything you have relevant — ECG, echocardiogram report, Holter report, stress test report, recent lab results, letters from previous cardiologists, list of your current cardiac medications. The more information your cardiologist provides, the more complete the evaluation will be.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the cardiologist adjust my medication?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including antihypertensive, antiarrhythmic, anticoagulant, diuretic medication, and other cardiac medications where clinically indicated, at the specialist’s discretion after a complete evaluation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the cardiologist request an echocardiogram or Holter monitor?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Where these tests are clinically indicated, your cardiologist issues the request on the same day. Private echocardiography and Holter monitoring are available in cardiology clinics and private hospitals throughout Spain — in many cities with availability within a few days.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I get a second cardiological opinion?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. A specialized cardiology second opinion is one of the common uses of this service — especially regarding uncertain diagnoses, test findings that have not been well explained, or before committing to significant cardiology interventions.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service suitable for pre-sport cardiovascular evaluation?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — for adults who want to start intense physical activity or have sports-related cardiology concerns. The official sports medical examination for federation licenses requires an in-person physical examination — but the pre-sport cardiology evaluation at the specialist medicine level can be carried out with review of tests by telemedicine.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-pay service. The clinical documentation issued is provided at the full private price regardless of insurance status.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection, a device with a camera, and the ability to send your cardiology tests digitally before the consultation.

description: Need a doctor in Spain today — in English? Our OMC-registered doctors offer full GP consultations by secure video call with full clinical documentation issued same day. No registration required.

Book General Medical Consultation in Spain

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need a health card or SIP to use this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. This is a private direct-pay service. No health card, SIP, or Spanish medical insurance of any kind is required.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the doctor treat infections that require antibiotics?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — where clinically indicated after a complete evaluation of your symptoms. In Spain, it is mandatory to have a medical prescription to obtain antibiotics at a pharmacy. Your doctor evaluates your presentation and prescribes the appropriate treatment where the clinical evidence justifies it.

schemaFaqs.question: Is the clinical documentation valid throughout Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. The clinical documentation issued by our doctors — including private electronic prescriptions where indicated — is approved by the OMC and connected to Nodofarma, valid at any of the more than 22,000 pharmacies in the national territory.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I obtain medical leave through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Global Health doctors can issue a private medical certificate that certifies temporary incapacity. To access sick leave for temporary incapacity (IT) in the public system with financial benefits from Social Security, you need a primary care doctor in the SNS.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I renew a prescription from another European country?
schemaFaqs.answer: Our doctor evaluates your current treatment and, if clinically appropriate, issues the equivalent Spanish medical documentation. Bring your current documentation to the consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: How long does it take for the medical records to arrive?
schemaFaqs.answer: When it is clinically indicated, the documentation is issued on the same day as the consultation, usually within minutes.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera.

schemaFaqs.question: What languages is it available in?
schemaFaqs.answer: Spanish, English and Portuguese — depending on the doctor’s availability.

María Fernanda Ocampo Mora· CGCOM | 291409735Book online€39per consultation15-minute appointmentDoctor registered in SpainInstant confirmation by emailConsultation summary includedBook this serviceSecure checkout · payments processed by StripeAbout this serviceHealthcare in Spain for International Residents — The Access GapSpain has one of the strongest healthcare systems in Europe — but access for international residents and visitors involves several practical barriers.Public system access requires registration, a NIE number, and either social security contributions, EU residency status, or enrolment under the Convenio Especial. Getting a GP assigned through the public system takes time and documentation — and until you are registered, you have no routine access to the public system for non-emergency care.Private clinics in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, and Málaga often have English-speaking doctors — but this is not guaranteed everywhere, appointments often require waiting days or weeks, and the cost of private in-person consultations typically ranges from €80 to €150.English-language telemedicine closes this gap — for the time between arriving and being fully registered, for acute issues that cannot wait for a clinic appointment, and for the significant proportion of international residents who prefer to consult in English regardless of their registration status.Our OMC-registered doctors consult in English by secure video call — same day, from anywhere in Spain — with full clinical documentation issued the same day.What We Can Help WithOur doctors assess and manage a wide range of acute and non-urgent No rushed appointment, no language barrier.Clinical documentation — at the doctor's professional discretionYour doctor issues appropriate clinical documentation following full assessment. This may include a private electronic prescription in accordance with Real Decreto 1718/2010, validated by the OMC and connected through Nodofarma to Spain's 22,000 pharmacies — where clinically indicated. You present your ID at any pharmacy of your choice anywhere in Spain.A private prescription in Spain is valid for 10 days from the date of issue for the first dispensation. You pay the full retail price of the medication — drug prices in Spain are government-regulated and generally very affordable.Antibiotics — assessment and treatment where clinically indicatedAll antibiotics in Spain require a doctor's prescription by law. Your doctor assesses your symptoms and prescribes the appropriate treatment where the clinical evidence supports it — including for urinary tract infections, respiratory infections, and skin infections — in accordance with antibiotic stewardship guidelines.Medication continuation from another countryRan out of medication you take regularly from your home country? Your doctor reviews your current treatment and — where clinically appropriate — issues the equivalent Spanish clinical documentation. Bring your original packaging, the generic name of your medication, and any documentation you have.Referral letters and medical documentationWhen specialist referral, blood tests, imaging, or other clinical documentation is needed, your doctor issues this the same day.How Medication Works in SpainSpain operates one of the most advanced private electronic prescription systems in Europe. description: Rash, eczema, acne, or skin concern in Spain? Our OMC-registered GPs assess skin conditions by secure video call. Clinical assessment same day anywhere in Spain, in English.
h1: Skin Consultation — GP Assessment Online, Same Day in Spain
h2: GP Skin Consultation vs. Specialist Dermatology Consultation
Moles and Skin Lesions — When to Act Promptly
Skin Conditions in Spain — A Note for Visitors and Expats

schemaFaqs.question: Can a skin condition really be evaluated by video call?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — for the vast majority of presentations. Dermatology is one of the medical specialties best suited to visual assessment, and a video consultation allows your GP to observe the condition directly. Where a condition cannot be adequately assessed at general practice level, your GP refers you to our specialist dermatology service within the same platform.

schemaFaqs.question: What is the difference between this consultation and the specialist dermatology consultation?
schemaFaqs.answer: This consultation is carried out by registered primary care physicians and covers most acute and non-urgent skin conditions. The specialist dermatology consultation is carried out by registered dermatologists from Global Health and is appropriate for complex conditions, treatment-resistant conditions, or those requiring high-resolution dermoscopy, consideration of isotretinoin, or coordinated biopsy. For most people who cannot manage their weight, there are underlying medical, hormonal, and metabolic factors at play that no generic diet plan addresses — because they require clinical assessment, not just calorie counting. Our doctors, registered with the Spanish Medical Council (OMC — Organización Médica Colegial), offer comprehensive weight management assessments by secure video call — identifying the clinical factors contributing to your weight, building a personalised management plan, and providing the medical supervision that makes sustainable change possible. Same day, from anywhere in Spain, in English, Spanish, or Portuguese. This is not a diet programme. It is medical care, provided by doctors, for a medical condition.Registered doctors · SpainSecure video consultationConfidential & GDPR-compliantClinically reviewed by Dra. María Fernanda Ocampo Mora· CGCOM | 291409735Book online€45per consultation15-minute appointmentDoctor registered in SpainInstant confirmation by emailConsultation summary includedBook this serviceSecure checkout · payments processed by StripeAbout this serviceWho This Service Is ForThis consultation is appropriate for adults who:Have difficulty losing weight despite dietary and lifestyle changesHave a BMI of 25 or above and are seeking structured medical supportHave weight-related conditions — including pre-diabetes, insulin resistance, hypertension, or PCOS — that are contributing to or complicating their weightWant to understand whether they may be candidates for medical weight management approaches following clinical assessmentHave tried diet and exercise approaches without sustainable resultsWant ongoing medical monitoring of their metabolic health alongside weight managementAre expats or international residents in Spain who want weight management support in English or PortugueseWhy Medical Supervision Makes a DifferenceMost weight management attempts fail not through lack of effort but because they do not address the underlying clinical picture. Hormonal imbalance, insulin resistance, medication side effects, sleep disorders, and metabolic dysfunction all contribute to weight gain in ways that diet and exercise alone cannot resolve.Specifically:Insulin resistance causes the body to store fat regardless of caloric deficitHypothyroidism slows metabolism — often significantly — independent of dietPCOS disrupts hormonal balance and makes weight loss genuinely more difficultCortisol dysregulation affects how the body distributes fatMedication side effects — antidepressants, antipsychotics, corticosteroids, beta-blockers — can cause significant weight gain as a direct pharmacological effectA plan that ignores these factors will fail — not because of insufficient effort, but because it is solving the wrong problem. Medical assessment identifies the specific causes and builds a plan that works with your biology.What Your Consultation IncludesComprehensive medical assessmentYour doctor reviews your medical history, current medications, metabolic risk factors, hormonal profile, dietary patterns, physical activity, sleep quality, stress levels, and previous weight management attempts — building a complete clinical picture of the factors contributing to your weight.Identification of underlying causesYour doctor assesses hormonal contributors — including thyroid dysfunction, insulin resistance, PCOS, and cortisol dysregulation — metabolic factors, medication-related weight gain, and lifestyle elements that interact with your biology.Personalised weight management planBased on the assessment, your doctor develops a structured, evidence-based plan adapted to your BMI, health status, lifestyle, and long-term goals — including nutritional strategy, behavioural approach, metabolic health optimisation, and clinical recommendations at the doctor's professional discretion.Assessment for medical weight management approachesFor patients who meet the clinical criteria, your doctor assesses suitability for evidence-based medical weight management approaches as part of a comprehensive clinical assessment. description: Want to stop smoking with medical support in Spain? Our OMC-registered GPs assess your tobacco dependence and create a personalised plan by video call. Same-day appointments available anywhere in Spain.
h1: Smoking Cessation — Medical Assessment and Personalised Plan in Spain
h2: Why Medical Support Makes the Difference
Stopping Smoking and Your Health — Why Now

schemaFaqs.question: Can my general practitioner help me quit smoking?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Smoking cessation is an integral part of primary care. Your primary care physician assesses your level of dependence, designs a personalized plan, and — where clinically indicated after a full evaluation — may consider pharmacological support options. Structured medical support significantly multiplies the chances of success compared with trying without support.

schemaFaqs.question: What pharmacological support options are available to quit smoking?
schemaFaqs.answer: There are various options for pharmacological support treatment for smoking cessation — including nicotine replacement therapy, bupropion, cytisine, and varenicline — with different profiles of efficacy, tolerability, and contraindications. The most appropriate option for you depends on your complete clinical profile. None can be confirmed or recommended before medical evaluation.

schemaFaqs.question: Are these treatments funded by Social Security?
schemaFaqs.answer: Since June 2024, certain medications for smoking cessation are funded by the Ministry of Health for patients who meet specific clinical criteria — including smokers with high dependence. Funding through the public system requires a prescription from an SNS doctor. Your Global Health doctor will inform you during the consultation if you may meet the criteria and what steps to follow.

schemaFaqs.question: How many consultations will I need?
schemaFaqs.answer: A structured smoking cessation plan generally includes an initial assessment and planning appointment, and follow-up appointments during the process — usually at 2 weeks, 1 month, and 3 months. Your doctor designs the appropriate follow-up schedule for your case.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if I have tried to quit smoking before and relapsed?
schemaFaqs.answer: Relapse is a normal part of the recovery process — it does not indicate failure, but rather that the plan needs to be adjusted. Previous unsuccessful attempts are clinically relevant information that your doctor uses to design a more effective approach. The more previous attempts there are, the more important structured medical support becomes.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service if I have health conditions such as diabetes or cardiovascular disease?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — and for these patients quitting smoking is especially a priority. Your doctor evaluates your complete clinical profile when designing the plan, including possible interactions with your current medication and the specific considerations of your health condition.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service suitable during pregnancy or breastfeeding?
schemaFaqs.answer: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding and want to quit smoking, consult your doctor at the start of the appointment. The support options available during pregnancy are different — your doctor will advise you on the safest approach for your situation.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-payment service. The clinical documentation issued through this service is provided at the full private price regardless of insurance status.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera.

description: Need a specialist referral letter, blood tests, or imaging in Spain? Our OMC-registered GPs issue clinical documentation after full assessment. Same-day appointments available anywhere in Spain.
h1: Referrals & Investigations — Clinical Documentation Online, Same Day

Why a Referral Letter Adds Value
Blood Tests — What Can Be Requested
Accessing Private Blood Tests in Spain

schemaFaqs.question: Can I obtain a referral letter without a full clinical evaluation?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Referral letters are issued after a complete clinical evaluation. Your doctor needs to assess your symptoms and medical history in order to write a clinically meaningful referral letter. A referral letter without a clinical evaluation would not add value to your specialist appointment.

schemaFaqs.question: Can this service provide referrals from the public SNS system?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Referrals in Spain’s public system require a primary care doctor contracted with the SNS. Global Health provides private referral letters for access to private specialists.

schemaFaqs.question: Does the referral letter have to be in Spanish?
schemaFaqs.answer: For Spanish-speaking specialists, yes — the referral letter is issued in Spanish. For English-speaking providers or international specialists, it can be issued in English. Your doctor issues it in the appropriate language based on whom you are going to see — mention it during the consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: How long do the test results take to arrive?
schemaFaqs.answer: Response times vary depending on the test — most standard analyses are available within 24 to 72 hours from private collection centers in Spain. Some specialized panels take longer. Your doctor advises you on the expected turnaround time when issuing the request.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service if I have Spanish private health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — but this service covers private referrals and private investigation requests. Your private medical insurance may cover specialist appointments and tests depending on your specific policy — check with your insurer. Tests and specialist appointments booked through this service are billed at the full private price regardless of your insurance.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if my results show something serious?
schemaFaqs.answer: If the review of your results reveals findings that require urgent attention, your doctor will advise you immediately on the appropriate next steps — including whether emergency care is needed. If emergency care is needed, call 112 or go to the nearest emergency department immediately.

schemaFaqs.question: What is the difference between this consultation and the skin consultation with the primary care physician?
schemaFaqs.answer: The skin consultation with a primary care doctor covers most acute and non-urgent skin conditions at the general medicine level — eczema, mild to moderate acne, rashes, infections. This specialist consultation is carried out by a registered dermatologist from Global Health and provides the depth of specialist analysis required for complex presentations — severe acne, suspicious lesions with dermatoscopic analysis, complex psoriasis, conditions that have not responded to standard treatments. If you are not sure which one you need, start with the primary care doctor consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can a dermatologist really evaluate a suspicious lesion by video call?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — with high-resolution image analysis, a dermatologist can perform a detailed, high-quality dermoscopic evaluation. This does not replace in-person dermoscopy with a contact dermoscope for lesions with high clinical suspicion — where the dermatologist coordinates an urgent in-person referral on the same day. But for the initial assessment of concerning lesions, specialized image analysis provides a clinically significantly superior evaluation compared with a general consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the dermatologist start treatment for severe acne?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including evaluation for specialized treatments where clinically indicated. All treatments are decided exclusively at the specialist’s discretion after a complete clinical evaluation. No specific treatment can be confirmed before the consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: How does follow-up work for treatments that require monitoring?
schemaFaqs.answer: For treatments that require clinical monitoring — control lab tests, response assessment, side effect monitoring — your dermatologist coordinates the complete follow-up schedule. Control lab tests can be requested online, with the results reviewed in a follow-up video consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the dermatologist coordinate a biopsy?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Where the biopsy is clinically indicated, your dermatologist issues the in-person referral documentation the same day — with a complete clinical report that maximizes the quality of the in-person evaluation.

schemaFaqs.question: I have psoriasis and topical treatments are not working for me — can this service help me?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. The evaluation for systemic treatments in moderate to severe psoriasis — including oral and biologic treatments where indicated — is a central part of this service. Your dermatologist assesses your treatment history, the extent and severity of your psoriasis, and the next-line options available.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I get a specialized dermatological second opinion?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. A specialized dermatological second opinion is one of the common uses of this service — especially for uncertain diagnoses, conditions that do not respond to treatment, or before committing to significant treatments.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-pay service. The clinical documentation issued is provided at the full private rate regardless of insurance status.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera, plus the ability to send high-resolution images before the consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: How is this different from a treatment renewal?
schemaFaqs.answer: Treatment Renewal is a one-off consultation for a stable condition — renewing a treatment that is working well. Chronic Disease follow-up is ongoing care — a doctor who knows your case over time, monitors your condition, adjusts management when necessary, and is involved in your long-term health.

schemaFaqs.question: How often will I need to have a consultation?
schemaFaqs.answer: It depends on your condition and how well controlled it is. For stable and well-controlled conditions, a quarterly or semiannual review is generally appropriate. For less well-controlled or more complex conditions, more frequent review is needed. Your doctor will advise you on the appropriate review schedule at the first consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the doctor access my Spanish medical history?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The doctors at Global Health do not have access to the electronic medical record system of the Spanish public health system. Please bring any relevant medical documentation — previous blood test results, specialist letters, imaging reports, and a list of your current medication — to your first appointment.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if I need a specialist?
schemaFaqs.answer: When specialized evaluation is needed, your doctor issues a formal referral letter and advises you on access to the appropriate specialist in Spain. Access to private specialists is generally straightforward in Spain’s major cities — Global Health coordinates this as part of ongoing follow-up.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service if I have a primary care doctor in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Some patients use Global Health for follow-up consultations for chronic diseases in English or Portuguese alongside their Spanish GP record — especially for conditions where they want to discuss management in detail in a language they fully understand.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if I need emergency care for my chronic illness?
schemaFaqs.answer: The management of chronic disease emergencies — hypertensive crisis, diabetic emergency, acute cardiac event — requires immediate emergency care. Call 112 or go to the nearest emergency department immediately. Ongoing follow-up through Global Health is for non-urgent chronic disease care.

schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-pay service. The clinical documentation issued through this service is dispensed at the full private price regardless of insurance status.

title: Medical Certificate Online Spain | Sick Note | English Doctor
description: Need a medical certificate or sick note in Spain today? Our OMC-registered doctors assess your symptoms by video call and issue private medical certificates where clinically justified. Same-day, in English.
h1: Medical Certificate in Spain — Online Assessment, Same Day
h2: How Sick Leave Works in Spain — What Expats and Tourists Need to Know

schemaFaqs.question: Does a private medical certificate have legal validity?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. A private medical certificate issued by a licensed physician has full legal validity as a clinical document. Most employers accept it to justify work absences, especially short-term ones. For the economic benefit for temporary disability from Social Security, the official sick note from the SNS or the mutual insurance company is required.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service if I am self-employed?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Self-employed workers do not have access to the same sick leave process as salaried employees. The private medical certificate clinically documents your health condition. If you contribute for common contingencies, check with your collaborating mutual insurance provider on how to manage sick leave — the doctor can guide you.

schemaFaqs.question: Does the certificate specify the diagnosis?
schemaFaqs.answer: The certificate documents the clinical evaluation and the assessment of temporary incapacity for work. If you prefer that the specific diagnosis not appear — for privacy reasons — mention it to the doctor at the start of the consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I obtain a retroactive certificate?
schemaFaqs.answer: Not routinely. Our doctors cannot clinically certify a period of illness that they did not evaluate at the time. If you have been sick for days, mention it at the start of the consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Does my company have to accept the private medical certificate?
schemaFaqs.answer: The legal obligation depends on the collective bargaining agreement and the internal policy of each company. In general, most employers accept private medical certificates for short-term absences.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I make a reservation if I have been sick for several days?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — but mention from the start of the consultation how many days you have had symptoms. The doctor will assess your current clinical situation and advise you on the most appropriate documentation for your case.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera.

schemaFaqs.question: What languages is it available in?
schemaFaqs.answer: Spanish, English and Portuguese — depending on the doctor’s availability.

title: Travel Health Online Spain | Malaria Prophylaxis | English Doctor
description: Travelling from Spain to a malaria zone or higher-risk destination? Our OMC-registered GPs assess travel health risks and manage clinical documentation for malaria prophylaxis. Same-day appointments in English.
h1: Travel Health Consultation — Medical Assessment Before You Go
h2: What a Pre-Travel Medical Consultation Provides That a Vaccination Centre Cannot
Spain as Both Origin and Destination — A Unique Travel Health Context
How Far in Advance Should I Book

schemaFaqs.question: I need antimalarials — can I manage it through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. The evaluation of antimalarial prophylaxis is one of the main reasons for using this service. Your primary care doctor evaluates the most appropriate antimalarial for your destination, itinerary, and health profile — and issues the clinical documentation directly. You present it at any pharmacy of your choice in Spain.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I obtain the yellow fever certificate through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Yellow fever vaccination and the International Certificate of Vaccination must be administered and issued in person at an authorized vaccination center. Your doctor advises you on which destinations require this certification and directs you to the appropriate authorized center in Spain after your consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can vaccines be administered during the consultation?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. This is a clinical evaluation and planning service. Vaccine administration requires an in-person visit to a vaccination center. Your doctor advises you on which vaccines you need and where to go — so that you arrive at the vaccination center with a clear plan.

schemaFaqs.question: What do I need to bring to my appointment?
schemaFaqs.answer: Your travel itinerary, destination details, planned activities, departure date, and any existing vaccination records. If you have a vaccination card from previous trips, bring it — your doctor will review it in full.

schemaFaqs.question: How far in advance should I book?
schemaFaqs.answer: Ideally four to six weeks before departure. For last-minute trips, book as soon as possible — your doctor will advise you on what is feasible.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service if I have become ill after traveling?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Post-travel evaluation is available. If you return from a higher-risk destination with symptoms — especially fever — book promptly. Certain tropical diseases require early diagnosis and treatment.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service suitable for families with children?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Travel health planning for families with children is a central part of this service.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the doctor issue a letter for the medication I am taking?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Your doctor issues a travel health summary letter documenting your medication, conditions, and medical devices — useful for customs, border health authorities, and airline requirements.

schemaFaqs.question: I have diabetes — is this service relevant to me?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes, especially. Managing diabetes during travel — insulin storage, time zone adjustment for dosing, dietary considerations, and when to seek care abroad — requires specific medical advice that a vaccination center cannot provide.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-pay service. The clinical documentation issued through this service is provided at the full private price regardless of insurance status.

If you return from a higher-risk destination with symptoms — especially fever — book promptly. Certain tropical diseases require early diagnosis and treatment.Is this service suitable for families with children?Yes. Travel health planning for families with children is a central part of this service.Can the doctor issue a letter for the medication I am taking?Yes. Managing diabetes during travel — insulin storage, time zone adjustment for dosing, dietary considerations, and when to seek care abroad — requires specific medical advice that a vaccination center cannot provide.Do I need Spanish health insurance?No. It is a private direct-pay service. description: Back pain, joint pain, sciatica, or muscle injury in Spain? Our OMC-registered GPs assess musculoskeletal conditions by secure video call. Clinical assessment same day anywhere in Spain, in English.
h1: Musculoskeletal Assessment — Online, Same Day in Spain
h2: Red Flags — When to Seek Emergency Care
Why Early Clinical Assessment Makes a Difference

schemaFaqs.question: Can a musculoskeletal condition really be evaluated by video call?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — for the vast majority of cases. The medical history is the most powerful diagnostic tool in musculoskeletal medicine, and a complete history can be taken by video call. Your doctor also observes your movement, posture, and functional ability during the call. Where physical examination findings are needed that cannot be assessed remotely, your doctor advises you on appropriate in-person evaluation.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if I need an MRI or X-ray?
schemaFaqs.answer: If imaging tests are clinically indicated based on the evaluation, your doctor issues an imaging request the same day. You can book the imaging at a private radiology center of your choice in Spain — private radiology is widely available in major cities and in many regional centers.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I get a referral to physiotherapy through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Referral letters to physiotherapy are issued when they are clinically indicated — addressed to the physiotherapist or clinic of your choice. Your doctor can advise you on what to look for in a physiotherapist for your specific condition.

schemaFaqs.question: What is cauda equina syndrome and why is it mentioned?
schemaFaqs.answer: Cauda equina syndrome is a rare but serious spinal emergency that presents as back pain associated with a change in bladder or bowel function. If you have back pain with any change in bladder or bowel function, go to the nearest emergency department immediately.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service suitable for sports injuries?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Sports and exercise-related musculoskeletal injuries are a central part of this service — including acute injuries, overuse conditions, and return-to-sport assessment after injury.

schemaFaqs.question: I already have imaging test results — can the doctor review them?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Bring any existing imaging test results, reports, or clinical letters to your appointment. Your doctor reviews them in full and incorporates the findings into the management plan.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need to have had imaging tests before booking?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Your doctor evaluates whether imaging tests are clinically indicated and orders them where appropriate. If you already have images, bring the results — your doctor reviews them in full.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service without a primary care doctor in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. This service is available to anyone in Spain — no prior registration, no primary care doctor required, no health insurance needed.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-payment service. The clinical documentation and referrals issued through this service are accepted on a private basis regardless of insurance status.

Waiting weeks for a traumatology or orthopaedic appointment for a condition that needs assessment today is a structural problem across both public and private healthcare in Spain. postural painErgonomic assessment and adviceSports and exercise-related injury assessmentWhat Your Consultation IncludesFull clinical assessmentYour GP takes a detailed history of your pain — onset, location, character, intensity, radiation, aggravating and relieving factors, functional impact, and systematic screening for red flags. Your GP assesses these as a standard part of every consultation.Personalised management planBased on the assessment, your GP advises on the most appropriate approach — which may include structured physiotherapy and rehabilitation referral, imaging requests where clinically indicated, specialist referral where needed, ergonomic and lifestyle advice, and clinical recommendations at the doctor's professional discretion.Clinical documentation — at the doctor's professional discretionWhen clinically indicated, your GP issues appropriate clinical documentation valid at any pharmacy in Spain.Note: Controlled substances and certain narcotics cannot be issued electronically under Spanish law. Our GPs do not routinely manage controlled substances through video consultations.Referral and investigation coordinationWhen physiotherapy referral, imaging, or specialist input is clinically indicated, your GP issues the relevant documentation the same day — so you leave the consultation with a clear clinical pathway.Red Flags — When to Seek Emergency CareMusculoskeletal pain is almost always benign — but some presentations require urgent assessment that cannot wait for a video consultation.Seek emergency care immediately if your pain is accompanied by:Any change in bladder or bowel function associated with back pain — incontinence or retention — this may indicate cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergencySignificant trauma — fall from height, road traffic accident, or significant impactSudden severe chest pain — which may indicate a cardiac or aortic cause rather than musculoskeletalUnexplained weight loss associated with new or worsening painFever associated with swelling and joint pain — may indicate septic arthritisRapidly progressive neurological symptoms — weakness, numbness, or loss of coordinationIf in doubt, always seek emergency care.Why Early Clinical Assessment Makes a DifferenceMost musculoskeletal conditions are self-limiting — they resolve with adequate rest, activity modification, and structured rehabilitation. But without clinical assessment, patients frequently either under-treat — returning to activity too early — or over-treat — restricting activity unnecessarily and prolonging recovery.Early clinical assessment identifies what is actually happening, excludes serious underlying pathology, and provides a structured, evidence-based management plan that allows full functional recovery more quickly and safely than waiting for the situation to resolve itself.Physiotherapy Access in SpainPrivate physiotherapy in Spain is widely available — but most physiotherapists require a referral letter or medical report to begin treatment. It presents as back pain associated with change in bladder or bowel function — including incontinence or difficulty urinating — and requires emergency surgical assessment.It is mentioned prominently on this page because it can initially be confused with common back pain. title: Paediatric GP Online Spain | Children's Doctor | Same Day
description: Child unwell in Spain? Our OMC-registered GPs assess children's health concerns by secure video call. No waiting room, same-day appointments available anywhere in Spain, in English.
h1: Paediatric GP Consultation — Children's Doctor Online, Same Day in Spain
h2: Paediatric Healthcare in Spain — How This Service Fits
When to Go to the Emergency Department — A Clear Guide for Parents

schemaFaqs.question: Can a child’s illness really be assessed by video call?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — for the vast majority of non-urgent presentations. A detailed parental history of the symptoms combined with visual observation of the child during the call allows an experienced doctor to make a clinical assessment of most common childhood illnesses. Where the presentation requires an in-person physical examination — for example, to assess breathing sounds, examine the ear, or palpate the abdomen — your doctor will clearly advise you and coordinate the appropriate referral.

schemaFaqs.question: My child has a fever — can I use this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — for children older than 3 months. Your doctor evaluates the severity, the likely cause, and the appropriate management. For infants under 3 months, fever is a medical emergency — go to the nearest emergency department immediately without booking a video consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the doctor prescribe antibiotics for my child?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — where clinically indicated after a complete evaluation. In Spain, all antibiotics require a medical prescription. Your doctor evaluates your child's presentation and prescribes the appropriate antibiotic where clinical evidence justifies it.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need to have an assigned pediatrician to use this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. This service is available to all families in Spain — no prior registration, no assigned pediatrician required, no health insurance necessary.

schemaFaqs.question: My child has received a letter or diagnosis from a Spanish pediatrician that I do not understand — can you help me?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Bring the letter or results to the appointment and your doctor will review and explain the findings and clinical recommendations clearly in the language you prefer.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service suitable for adolescents?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Adolescents’ health concerns — including acne, menstrual health, mental well-being and weight — are part of this service. For adolescents aged 16 or older, the doctor assesses whether the young person can consent independently. For those under 16, a parent or guardian must be present throughout the consultation.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if my child needs to go to the emergency room?
schemaFaqs.answer: If your doctor determines that your child needs urgent or in-person urgent care, you will be informed immediately and clearly — including what to say when you arrive at the emergency department and which hospital is most appropriate for your location in Spain. Your doctor may issue a brief clinical summary if this would be useful.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I obtain a school absence note through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. School absence certificates may be issued at the clinician’s discretion after evaluation — certifying that the child was evaluated and is not fit to attend school, without specifying clinical details.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-pay service. The clinical documentation issued through this service is provided at the full private price regardless of insurance status.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera.

schemaFaqs.question: What is the difference between a psychologist and a psychiatrist?
schemaFaqs.answer: The clinical psychologist provides psychotherapy and psychological intervention — does not prescribe medication. The psychiatrist is a medical specialist who can formally diagnose mental disorders and prescribe psychiatric medication. For many people, working with both together is the most effective approach. If you need pharmacological evaluation or psychiatric medication management, our specialist psychiatry service is the appropriate one.

schemaFaqs.question: How many sessions will I need?
schemaFaqs.answer: It depends on your presentation and your goals. Some problems are effectively addressed in 8–12 sessions with approaches such as CBT. Others — work on complex trauma, personality patterns, or more deeply rooted conditions — require longer-term work. Your psychologist will propose an initial plan in the first consultation and review it with you regularly.

schemaFaqs.question: How often are the sessions?
schemaFaqs.answer: Generally once a week at the start of therapeutic work, moving to every two weeks or monthly in more advanced phases. Your psychologist adjusts the frequency to your situation and progress.

schemaFaqs.question: Is online psychotherapy covered by Spanish private health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: It depends on your policy. Some private insurance plans cover online psychology consultations — check with your insurer and request the invoice we issue after each session for reimbursement.

schemaFaqs.question: Does online therapy work the same as in-person therapy?
schemaFaqs.answer: Scientific evidence indicates that psychotherapy by video call has outcomes comparable to in-person therapy for most presentations. The therapeutic alliance — one of the most predictive factors of outcome — also develops online in the same way.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if I need medication in addition to psychotherapy?
schemaFaqs.answer: Your psychologist will clearly guide you if they consider that a psychiatric evaluation may be beneficial for your situation. Our specialist psychiatry service is available within the same platform — and both professionals can work in a coordinated way for your care.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I change psychologists if I don’t feel comfortable?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. The compatibility between the patient and the psychologist is important for the therapeutic outcome. If after the first sessions you do not feel comfortable, you can request to work with another psychologist on the team.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service appropriate if I am in crisis?

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service from anywhere in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including the Balearic Islands, the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. You only need a stable internet connection and a device with a camera.

The practical distinction is straightforward: if you want to talk in depth about what is happening and learn psychological tools to manage it, psychology is the right starting point. The therapeutic approaches our clinical psychologists use include:Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)The approach with the strongest scientific evidence for most anxiety disorders and depression. Works on the relationship between thoughts, emotions, and behaviours — identifying thought patterns that generate distress and developing more adaptive strategies.Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)A third-generation approach working on psychological flexibility — learning to relate differently to difficult thoughts and emotions, and acting in line with personal values even in the presence of distress.EMDR — Eye Movement Desensitisation and ReprocessingThe treatment with the strongest evidence for trauma and PTSD. Works on mindfulness skills, distress tolerance, emotional regulation, and interpersonal effectiveness.Brief Psychodynamic PsychotherapyUseful when current difficulties have roots in past experiences and relational patterns. Works on the meaning of symptoms and deeper understanding of recurring patterns.Mindfulness-based approachesIntegrated into several therapeutic frameworks, particularly useful for stress, anxiety, and burnout.The most appropriate therapeutic approach for you depends on your presentation, your goals, and your preferences. description: Complex mental health condition, ADHD, bipolar disorder, or psychiatric concern in Spain? Our specialist psychiatrists offer expert assessments by secure video call. Same-day appointments available in English.
h1: Specialist Psychiatry — Online Psychiatric Assessment in Spain
h2: GP Mental Health Assessment vs. Specialist Psychiatric Consultation
What This Service Is — And What It Is Not
Accessing Psychiatry in Spain — The Reality

schemaFaqs.question: What is the difference between seeing a psychiatrist and seeing a psychologist?
schemaFaqs.answer: The psychiatrist is a medical specialist with MIR training in psychiatry — they can formally diagnose mental disorders, prescribe psychiatric medication, and coordinate the complete care plan. The clinical psychologist provides psychotherapy — structured psychological intervention. For many conditions, the most effective approach combines both. Your psychiatrist advises you on the most appropriate level of support and can guide you on the most suitable type of psychotherapy for your condition.

schemaFaqs.question: What is the difference between this consultation and the mental health assessment with a primary care physician?
schemaFaqs.answer: Mental health evaluation with a general practitioner is appropriate for the initial screening of anxiety, mild to moderate depression, and stress — with referral to psychiatry where indicated. This specialist consultation is conducted by a psychiatrist and provides formal psychiatric diagnosis, evaluation of complex disorders such as bipolar disorder or ADHD, and access to the full range of psychiatric pharmacological treatment options.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the psychiatrist prescribe psychiatric medication through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — including antidepressants, mood stabilizers, ADHD medication, and other psychiatric pharmacological treatment options where clinically indicated. Benzodiazepines and certain controlled medications have specific requirements in Spain — your psychiatrist will inform you about the available options and any applicable limitations. No specific medication can be confirmed before the evaluation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the psychiatrist diagnose ADHD in adults?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. The formal diagnostic evaluation of ADHD in adults is a central part of this service. Diagnosis requires a complete structured assessment — it cannot be made in a single brief session. Your psychiatrist informs you about the appropriate diagnostic process for your presentation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the psychiatrist diagnose bipolar disorder?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. The differential diagnosis between unipolar depression and bipolar disorder, and between the different types of bipolar disorder, requires specialized psychiatric evaluation. It is one of the diagnoses most frequently missed or delayed in primary care — specialized psychiatric evaluation is especially valuable here.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I obtain a psychiatric second opinion through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. The specialized psychiatric second opinion is one of the frequent uses of this service — especially regarding diagnoses, treatment plans, or medication received from another psychiatrist.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the psychiatrist order my psychiatric hospital admission?
schemaFaqs.answer: Voluntary admission can be coordinated with the appropriate services. Involuntary admission is regulated by Article 763 of the Civil Procedure Act and requires judicial authorization — it cannot be initiated through this service. If your situation requires urgent admission, call 112 or go to the nearest emergency department immediately.
