For patients who most need psychiatric support, removing the access barrier matters.Confidentiality in Psychiatric CareEverything discussed during your psychiatric consultation is confidential and protected under Spanish and European data protection law — including Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) implemented through Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD) and Law 41/2002 on patient autonomy.Mental health data has reinforced protection as a special category of data under the GDPR.There are two circumstances in which confidentiality may need to be carefully considered — when there is serious and immediate risk to your life or safety, or when there is serious risk to the safety of another person. Your psychiatrist discusses confidentiality with you at the outset of the consultation.Start here¿Necesitas ayuda con evaluación inicial de salud mental?Para evaluación inicial de salud mental, consulta nuestra página de Salud Mental — evaluación clínica específica para tu caso.Salud MentalStart here¿Segunda opinión psiquiátrica independiente?Si tu situación está relacionada con segunda opinión psiquiátrica independiente, nuestra Segunda Opinión Médica te ofrece la evaluación adecuada.Segunda Opinión MédicaStart here¿Necesitas ayuda con evaluación inicial con médico de cabecera?Para evaluación inicial con médico de cabecera, consulta nuestra página de Consulta Médica General — evaluación clínica específica para tu caso.Consulta Médica GeneralRelated care¿Psicoterapia y apoyo psicológico?Si tu situación está relacionada con psicoterapia y apoyo psicológico, nuestra Psicología Clínica te ofrece la evaluación adecuada.Psicología ClínicaSpecialists in SpainSpecialists registered with national medical councils.View profile for Dra. Mónica Fabiana Cornejo RománRegistrationCGCOM | 64182LanguagesSpanishPick a timeView profileQuestionsFrequently Asked QuestionsWhat is the difference between seeing a psychiatrist and seeing a psychologist?The psychiatrist is a medical specialist with MIR training in psychiatry — they can formally diagnose mental disorders, prescribe psychiatric medication, and coordinate the complete care plan. The clinical psychologist provides psychotherapy — structured psychological intervention. For many conditions, the most effective approach combines both. Your psychiatrist advises you on the most appropriate level of support and can guide you on the most suitable type of psychotherapy for your condition.What is the difference between this consultation and the mental health assessment with a primary care physician?Mental health evaluation with a general practitioner is appropriate for the initial screening of anxiety, mild to moderate depression, and stress — with referral to psychiatry where indicated. This specialist consultation is conducted by a psychiatrist and provides formal psychiatric diagnosis, evaluation of complex disorders such as bipolar disorder or ADHD, and access to the full range of psychiatric pharmacological treatment options.Can the psychiatrist prescribe psychiatric medication through this service?Yes — including antidepressants, mood stabilizers, ADHD medication, and other psychiatric pharmacological treatment options where clinically indicated. Benzodiazepines and certain controlled medications have specific requirements in Spain — your psychiatrist will inform you about the available options and any applicable limitations. No specific medication can be confirmed before the evaluation.Can the psychiatrist diagnose ADHD in adults?Yes. The formal diagnostic evaluation of ADHD in adults is a central part of this service. Diagnosis requires a complete structured assessment — it cannot be made in a single brief session. Your psychiatrist informs you about the appropriate diagnostic process for your presentation.Can the psychiatrist diagnose bipolar disorder?Yes. The differential diagnosis between unipolar depression and bipolar disorder, and between the different types of bipolar disorder, requires specialized psychiatric evaluation. It is one of the diagnoses most frequently missed or delayed in primary care — specialized psychiatric evaluation is especially valuable here.Can I obtain a psychiatric second opinion through this service?Yes. Involuntary admission is regulated by Article 763 of the Civil Procedure Act and requires judicial authorization — it cannot be initiated through this service. If your situation requires urgent admission, call 112 or go to the nearest emergency department immediately.What happens if I am in crisis during or after the consultation?If you are in crisis, use the resources at the top of this page — Suicide Helpline 024 or 112 in case of immediate danger. schemaFaqs.answer: No. Renewal of treatment requires a clinical review. The doctor evaluates your current condition, response to treatment, and any changes since your last review before determining whether continuation is clinically appropriate.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I continue any medication?
schemaFaqs.answer: Most stable and established treatments managed by a general practitioner can be reviewed and continued through this service. schemaFaqs.question: How do I receive the clinical documentation?

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Private medical documentation is provided at the full private price. Spanish health insurance or a health card is not required.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if my condition has changed since my last review?
schemaFaqs.answer: If your symptoms have changed significantly, a general medical consultation is more appropriate. Your doctor will inform you during the consultation if a more detailed evaluation is necessary.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this a counseling or therapy service?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. This is a primary care-level clinical mental health evaluation. Our doctors assess your current mental health, provide clinical recommendations, and refer you to the appropriate level of support — including counseling, psychotherapy, or psychiatry where indicated. Counseling or psychotherapy sessions are not provided through this service.

schemaFaqs.question: What if I need to see a psychiatrist?
schemaFaqs.answer: If your evaluation indicates that psychiatric assessment is needed, your doctor clearly advises and coordinates the referral to the appropriate specialized service — including English-language psychiatric services in Spain where available.

schemaFaqs.question: Will my employer or someone else be informed?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Your consultation is completely confidential and is protected under Spanish and European data protection legislation. The information is not shared without your explicit consent, except in the very limited circumstances described in the confidentiality section above.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this service if I am already seeing a therapist?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. A general-practice-level mental health clinical assessment can complement ongoing psychological or therapeutic support — particularly where clinical recommendations, physical health assessment, or coordination of care are needed.

schemaFaqs.question: Is this service suitable for teenagers?
schemaFaqs.answer: Mental health consultations for patients under 16 years of age require the presence and consent of the parents or guardians. For adolescents 16 years of age or older, the doctor evaluates the capacity to consent individually.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if I am in crisis during or after the appointment?
schemaFaqs.answer: If you are in crisis, use the resources at the beginning of this page — Suicide Hotline 024 or 112 in case of immediate danger. This service is not a crisis intervention service.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I discuss ADHD concerns through this service?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Initial ADHD screening at the general medicine level is available through this service. A formal ADHD diagnosis requires specialist evaluation — your doctor advises on the appropriate referral pathway if the screening indicates that this is justified.

title: Second Medical Opinion Online Spain | Independent Assessment | Same Day
description: Not sure about a diagnosis or treatment plan in Spain? Our OMC-registered doctors provide independent second medical opinions by secure video call. Same-day appointments available anywhere in Spain.
h1: Second Medical Opinion — Independent Clinical Assessment in Spain
h2: When a Second Opinion Makes Sense
Second Opinions in Spain — Why They Matter
What a Second Opinion Can and Cannot Do
Book Second Medical Opinion in Spain

schemaFaqs.question: Does seeking a second opinion mean that I am questioning my doctor?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Seeking a second opinion is a normal and recommended part of good medical decision-making — especially for significant diagnoses or treatment recommendations. Most doctors expect and respect patients who seek independent review of major clinical decisions.

schemaFaqs.question: What documentation should I bring?
schemaFaqs.answer: Bring everything that is relevant — diagnostic letters, specialist reports, imaging test results, lab results, treatment plans, discharge summaries, and any other clinical documentation related to the concern. The more complete the documentation, the more useful the independent assessment will be.

schemaFaqs.question: Can the doctor review documentation in Spanish?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Your doctor reviews clinical documentation in Spanish and explains the findings clearly in English, Spanish, or Portuguese — according to your preference.

schemaFaqs.question: Will the second opinion doctor contact my current doctor?
schemaFaqs.answer: No — unless you specifically request it. The second opinion is provided directly to you. If you want the findings to be shared with your treating team, your doctor can issue a written clinical summary for this purpose.

schemaFaqs.question: What happens if the second opinion contradicts my current diagnosis?
schemaFaqs.answer: Your doctor explains the clinical reasoning clearly and honestly. If the independent evaluation suggests that the original diagnosis or treatment plan may not be the most appropriate, you are advised on what questions to ask your treating team and what additional steps — further investigation, specialist assessment — may be justified.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I get a second opinion on a surgical recommendation?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Second opinions on surgical recommendations are one of the most common and most valuable uses of this service. Your doctor reviews the clinical justification for the recommended surgery, discusses the evidence, and advises on whether the recommendation seems appropriate and what questions to ask your surgeon.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I get a second opinion on a mental health diagnosis?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes — for mental health conditions at the general medicine level. For complex psychiatric diagnoses, your doctor advises on the appropriate level of independent specialized review.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need Spanish health insurance?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is a private direct-pay service with no health insurance requirement.

title: ADHD Test Spain | Free Adult ADHD Screening · Global Health
description: Take the six-question adult ADHD screener (ASRS v1.1 Part A) and see what your answers mean. A screening result is not a diagnosis — only a psychiatrist or clinical psychologist can make one.
h2: What ADHD looks like in adults
What this screen cannot tell you
Want to talk your result through?

schemaFaqs.question: Can an online ADHD test diagnose ADHD?
schemaFaqs.answer: No, and no online questionnaire can. This is a screener: it sorts people into "worth assessing properly" and "not on these answers". A diagnosis is made by a psychiatrist or a clinical psychologist, from a full interview about your history rather than from six questions.

schemaFaqs.question: What is the ASRS?
schemaFaqs.answer: The Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale, developed with the World Health Organization. Part A is the six-question screener used here; the full scale has eighteen items. It is the most widely used adult ADHD screening instrument, which is why clinicians recognise the result you bring them.

schemaFaqs.question: What counts as a positive result?
schemaFaqs.answer: Four or more of the six questions answered at or above that question's own threshold. The first three count from "Sometimes", the last three only from "Often" — the thresholds differ because the questions do, and a single flat cut-off would miss the inattentive presentation.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I have ADHD if my result is negative?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Six questions cannot cover a condition that presents differently at different ages and in different people, and the inattentive presentation in particular is under-detected — one reason women are diagnosed later and less often. If the difficulties are affecting your life, a negative screen is not a reason to stop asking.

schemaFaqs.question: Who can diagnose ADHD?
schemaFaqs.answer: A psychiatrist or a clinical psychologist, depending on the country. A GP is normally where the process starts: they take the history, rule out the conditions that mimic ADHD — thyroid problems, sleep disorders, anxiety, depression — and refer you on for the assessment itself.

schemaFaqs.question: Does this ADHD test store my answers?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The scoring runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you select is sent to our servers or saved.

schemaFaqs.question: How is adult ADHD assessed in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: It starts in primary care: your family doctor reviews your history, rules out the conditions that look like ADHD — thyroid, sleep, anxiety, depression — and refers you to mental health services. The diagnosis is made by a psychiatrist or a clinical psychologist, never by a questionnaire.

schemaFaqs.question: Can an online test get me ADHD medication in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. ADHD medicines are controlled and are started only after a full specialist assessment and a diagnosis. Our registered doctors can review a screening result, check for the conditions that mimic ADHD and refer you onwards; a diagnosis is not something a video consultation can give you.

body: Free health toolADHD test SpainAnswer six questions about the last six months to see whether your answers match the pattern the adult ADHD screener looks for.The six-question ASRS v1.1 Part A screenerScored per question, the way the scale is designedRuns in your browser — nothing is sent or storedYour answersFor each question, choose how often it has applied to you over the past six months.How often do you leave the last details of a project unfinished once the hard part is behind you?NeverRarelySometimesOftenVery oftenHow often do you struggle to get things in order when a task needs organising?NeverRarelySometimesOftenVery oftenHow often do you forget appointments or commitments you had agreed to?NeverRarelySometimesOftenVery oftenHow often do you put off or avoid starting something that will take a lot of thought?NeverRarelySometimesOftenVery oftenHow often do you fidget with your hands or feet when you have to stay seated for a long time?NeverRarelySometimesOftenVery oftenHow often do you feel restlessly driven to keep doing things, as though something were pushing you along?NeverRarelySometimesOftenVery often0 / 6Screening result: negativeYour answers do not match the pattern this screener looks for. That does not rule ADHD out — six questions cover only part of it — so if these difficulties are affecting your work, your studies or your relationships, talk to a doctor anyway.Positive screen4 or more of 6This is a screening questionnaire, not a diagnosis. ADHD is diagnosed only by a psychiatrist or a clinical psychologist, after a full assessment. Nothing here is a recommendation for medication.01How the screen is scoredThe questions are Part A of the World Health Organization's Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale — the short form used to decide whether a full assessment is worth arranging, rather than the assessment itself.Scoring is per question, not a running total. Each item has its own threshold, and four or more items reaching their own threshold is a positive screen. Treating it as a flat "four answers of Often" rule is the usual mistake, and it misses the inattentive presentation, which is the one most often overlooked in adults.1What it asks aboutFinishing the last details of a projectCounts fromSometimes2What it asks aboutGetting things in order for a taskCounts fromSometimes3What it asks aboutRemembering appointments and commitmentsCounts fromSometimes4What it asks aboutPutting off tasks that take a lot of thoughtCounts fromOften5What it asks aboutFidgeting when you have to stay seatedCounts fromOften6What it asks aboutFeeling restlessly driven to keep goingCounts fromOftenThe six screening questions and the answer each one counts fromQuestionWhat it asks aboutCounts from1Finishing the last details of a projectSometimes2Getting things in order for a taskSometimes3Remembering appointments and commitmentsSometimes4Putting off tasks that take a lot of thoughtOften5Fidgeting when you have to stay seatedOften6Feeling restlessly driven to keep goingOftenFour or more questions at or above their own threshold is a positive screen. The scale was developed for adults from 18 onwards and is not a children's screener.02What ADHD looks like in adultsAdult ADHD rarely looks like the classroom picture. Hyperactivity often turns inward — restlessness, a mind that will not settle — while the inattentive side stays and gets expensive: missed deadlines, unopened admin, a working memory that keeps dropping things.What matters for a diagnosis is that the difficulties are long-standing, show up in more than one part of life, and cause real impairment. Everyone loses their keys occasionally; that is not what is being asked.Starting tasks that matter, and finishing the ones that have stopped being interesting.Time: underestimating it, losing it, arriving late despite genuinely trying not to.Organisation — paperwork, bills, appointments — costing far more effort than it seems to cost other people.Restlessness, or a constant low-level need to be doing something.Interrupting, blurting things out, or acting on an idea before thinking it through.Emotions that arrive fast and pass fast, often out of proportion to what caused them.03What this screen cannot tell youA six-question screener is a sorting tool. It is deliberately quick and deliberately over-inclusive, because its job is to decide who should be assessed properly — not to decide who has ADHD.It is not a diagnosis, and a positive result on its own means no more than "worth assessing".A negative result does not rule ADHD out, particularly for the inattentive presentation and particularly in women, who are diagnosed later and less often.Anxiety, depression, poor sleep, thyroid disease, chronic pain and heavy drinking all produce the same answers.It cannot separate ADHD from autism, from a specific learning difficulty, or from the effects of a long stretch of stress.It was designed and validated for adults. Children and teenagers need a different assessment entirely.It says nothing about treatment. Medication is one option among several, and it is only ever considered after a diagnosis.04Getting properly assessedA diagnosis of ADHD is made by a psychiatrist or a clinical psychologist. The assessment is a structured clinical interview covering your history from childhood onwards, usually with rating scales and, where possible, an account from someone who has known you a long time.Start with a doctor. They will go through your history, check for the conditions that look like ADHD, and refer you for assessment.Bring specifics rather than a score: school reports, work reviews, the things that keep going wrong and how long they have been going wrong for.Say what else is going on — sleep, mood, alcohol, thyroid, a past head injury. Those change both the assessment and the order it happens in.A screening result is a starting point for that conversation, not a substitute for it. Take yours with you.If you are struggling to cope, or having thoughts of harming yourself, contact a doctor or the emergency services now rather than waiting for an assessment.Where to go from hereA screening result is a reason to get assessed, not a diagnosis. title: Blood Pressure Chart Spain | What Your Reading Means
description: Check your systolic and diastolic numbers against the European adult blood pressure chart. See the category, what it means, and which readings need medical care the same day.
h2: How to take a reading worth trusting
What a single reading cannot tell you
When to see a doctor, and when to get help now
Want a doctor to look at your readings?

schemaFaqs.question: What is a normal blood pressure for an adult?
schemaFaqs.answer: Under 120/80 mmHg is optimal, and 120–129 over 80–84 is still classed as normal. From 130/85 a reading is high-normal, and 140/90 or above measured in a clinic is hypertension. Home monitors read lower, so the home threshold is 135/85.

schemaFaqs.question: Which number matters more, the top or the bottom?
schemaFaqs.answer: Both. The category is set by whichever number is worse, so 128/95 counts as grade 1 hypertension on the strength of the bottom number alone. Systolic pressure predicts cardiovascular risk better after about 50, diastolic before it.

schemaFaqs.question: What does an isolated systolic reading mean?
schemaFaqs.answer: A systolic of 140 or more with a diastolic under 90. It is the commonest pattern of high blood pressure after 60, caused by arteries stiffening with age, and it carries real cardiovascular risk — it is not a harmless quirk of the top number.

schemaFaqs.question: Can one high reading mean I have hypertension?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Hypertension is diagnosed from repeated raised readings, usually backed by a week of home measurements or a 24-hour monitor. A single high reading is a reason to measure again properly, not a diagnosis.

schemaFaqs.question: What blood pressure is dangerous?
schemaFaqs.answer: A reading of 180/120 or above needs medical attention the same day. If it comes with chest pain, weakness or numbness on one side, difficulty speaking or a sudden change in vision, call the emergency services immediately — those are symptoms of a heart attack or a stroke.

schemaFaqs.question: Does this blood pressure chart store my reading?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The comparison runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to our servers or saved.

schemaFaqs.question: What counts as high blood pressure in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Spanish practice follows the European thresholds: 140/90 mmHg or above in a clinic, or 135/85 or above on a validated home monitor. A single raised reading is not a diagnosis — a doctor will normally ask for a week of home readings, or 24-hour monitoring, first.

schemaFaqs.question: Where can I get my blood pressure checked in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Any medical appointment includes it, and most pharmacies will measure it too. Bring a week of home readings to a consultation and our registered doctors can review the whole set by video, alongside your cholesterol and blood glucose.

body: Free health toolBlood pressure chart SpainEnter the two numbers from your monitor to see where the reading sits on the European adult chart — and what, if anything, to do about it.European (ESC/ESH) adult categoriesFlags readings that need same-day careRuns in your browser — nothing is sent or storedYour readingSystolic (top number)mmHgDiastolic (bottom number)mmHg120/80mmHgNormalWithin the normal adult range. Worth re-checking now and again, especially if it has been drifting upwards.Where your systolic number sits90120140160180Optimal for most adultsBelow 120/80 mmHgThis chart is a screening reference, not a diagnosis. Hypertension is diagnosed from repeated readings, usually a week of home measurements or a 24-hour monitor, never from a single figure.01The adult blood pressure chartBlood pressure is written as two numbers: the systolic pressure while the heart contracts, over the diastolic pressure while it relaxes between beats. Both are measured in millimetres of mercury (mmHg).The categories below are the European ones (ESC/ESH). Where the two numbers fall into different categories, the higher category is the one that counts — 128/95 is grade 1 hypertension, not normal.LowSystolic (mmHg)Under 90Diastolic (mmHg)or under 60OptimalSystolic (mmHg)Under 120Diastolic (mmHg)and under 80NormalSystolic (mmHg)120 – 129Diastolic (mmHg)and/or 80 – 84High-normalSystolic (mmHg)130 – 139Diastolic (mmHg)and/or 85 – 89Grade 1 hypertensionSystolic (mmHg)140 – 159Diastolic (mmHg)and/or 90 – 99Grade 2 hypertensionSystolic (mmHg)160 – 179Diastolic (mmHg)and/or 100 – 109Grade 3 hypertensionSystolic (mmHg)180 or moreDiastolic (mmHg)and/or 110 or moreIsolated systolicSystolic (mmHg)140 or moreDiastolic (mmHg)and under 90European adult blood pressure categoriesCategorySystolic (mmHg)Diastolic (mmHg)LowUnder 90or under 60OptimalUnder 120and under 80Normal120 – 129and/or 80 – 84High-normal130 – 139and/or 85 – 89Grade 1 hypertension140 – 159and/or 90 – 99Grade 2 hypertension160 – 179and/or 100 – 109Grade 3 hypertension180 or moreand/or 110 or moreIsolated systolic140 or moreand under 90Clinic thresholds for adults. Home and 24-hour monitors read lower, so hypertension is 135/85 on a home device rather than 140/90. Pregnancy, childhood and dialysis use different targets entirely.02How to take a reading worth trustingMost alarming readings are measurement artefacts. Blood pressure moves through the day and jumps with a rushed arrival, a full bladder or a conversation mid-cuff, so how you measure changes the number more than people expect.Sit still for five minutes first — back supported, feet flat on the floor, legs uncrossed.No coffee, food, exercise or cigarettes for 30 minutes beforehand, and empty your bladder.Rest your arm on a table so the cuff sits level with your heart, against bare skin.Use a cuff that fits your arm. Too small a cuff reads high, and it is the commonest home-monitor error.Stay quiet while it inflates. Talking adds several mmHg.Take two readings a minute apart and use the second, or the average of the two.Measure morning and evening for seven days, then bring the whole set to a doctor.03What a single reading cannot tell youA reading is a snapshot of one moment in one arm. That is enough to flag a problem and not enough to name one, which is why a diagnosis rests on repeated readings rather than on the first alarming figure.White-coat hypertension: raised in a clinic, normal at home. Common, and only home or 24-hour monitoring separates it out.Masked hypertension: normal in the clinic, raised the rest of the time. The riskier of the two, and invisible without home readings.Arms differ. A gap of more than 10 mmHg between them matters, and the higher arm is the one to use from then on.An irregular pulse, atrial fibrillation included, makes most automatic monitors unreliable.Not every home device is clinically validated, and an unvalidated one can be out by a wide margin.Pregnancy has its own thresholds and its own risks. schemaFaqs.question: What is a healthy BMI for an adult?
schemaFaqs.answer: For most adults aged 18 to 65, the World Health Organization considers a BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 to be the healthy range. Above 25 is classed as overweight and 30 or above as obesity. These are population thresholds, so a single reading is a prompt to look further, not a verdict.

schemaFaqs.question: Is BMI calculated differently for men and women?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The formula and the adult categories are identical. Women generally carry a higher proportion of body fat than men at the same BMI, which is one of the reasons the number is only a starting point.

schemaFaqs.question: How accurate is a BMI calculator?
schemaFaqs.answer: The arithmetic is exact — the uncertainty is in what BMI measures. It correlates reasonably well with body fat across a population but can misclassify individuals, particularly athletes, older adults and people with a lot of muscle.

schemaFaqs.question: What should I do if my BMI is in the obese range?
schemaFaqs.answer: Have your blood pressure, cholesterol and blood glucose checked, and talk to a doctor about a plan you can actually sustain. Weight management that includes medical review works considerably better than dieting alone.

schemaFaqs.question: Does this BMI calculator store my details?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The calculation runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to our servers or saved.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need a BMI to get weight-loss treatment?
schemaFaqs.answer: Clinicians normally use BMI as one of the entry criteria for weight management programmes, usually alongside your medical history and any weight-related conditions. Your doctor will confirm what applies to you.

schemaFaqs.question: Does the Spanish health system use BMI?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. BMI is the first-line screening measure in Spanish practice, as it is internationally — read alongside waist circumference, blood pressure and blood tests rather than on its own. A raised BMI prompts further assessment; it is not a diagnosis by itself.

schemaFaqs.question: Where can I get my BMI checked in Spain?

title: Calorie Calculator Spain | Daily Calorie Needs
description: Work out how many calories you need a day to maintain, lose or gain weight. Mifflin-St Jeor equation, five activity levels, and what the numbers actually mean — with registered doctors if you want to go further.
h2: What a calorie calculator cannot tell you
Want a plan, not just a number?

schemaFaqs.question: How many calories should I eat a day?
schemaFaqs.answer: Enough to match what you burn, if your weight is where you want it. For most adults that lands somewhere between 1,800 and 2,800 kcal, but the range is wide because it depends on your size, age and how active you are. The calculator above gives your own figure rather than the average.

schemaFaqs.question: How many calories do I need to eat to lose weight?
schemaFaqs.answer: About 500 kcal a day below your maintenance figure gives roughly half a kilo a week, and 250 below gives about a quarter of a kilo. Bigger deficits do not reliably work faster — they are simply harder to keep, and more of the loss comes from muscle.

schemaFaqs.question: Is 1,200 calories a day safe?
schemaFaqs.answer: It is the lowest intake this calculator will suggest, and it is a floor rather than a recommendation. Below roughly that level it becomes difficult to get enough protein, vitamins and minerals from food, so a lower intake should only be followed under medical supervision.

schemaFaqs.question: Which formula does this calorie calculator use?
schemaFaqs.answer: Mifflin-St Jeor for the basal rate, then a standard activity multiplier. It replaced the older Harris-Benedict equation in most clinical use because it is more accurate for modern body compositions, typically to within about 10% for healthy adults.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I have to count calories to lose weight?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Counting is one method of holding a deficit, and plenty of people manage the same thing by changing what they eat rather than by weighing it. Knowing roughly where your maintenance level sits is useful either way, because it tells you how big a change you are actually making.

schemaFaqs.question: Does this calorie calculator store my details?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The calculation runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to our servers or saved.

schemaFaqs.question: How many calories a day are recommended in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Spanish food labels carry the EU reference intake of 2,000 kcal a day for an average adult, and the national healthy-eating advice is built around figures of that order. They are population averages — your own needs depend on height, weight, age and activity, which is what the calculator above estimates.

schemaFaqs.question: Can a doctor in Spain review my calorie target?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. A consultation can check whether the figure suits your history and refer you for a full eating plan when one is needed. Our registered doctors can review it by video alongside your blood pressure, cholesterol and blood glucose.

title: Due Date Calculator Spain | Pregnancy Week by Week
description: Work out your estimated due date and how many weeks pregnant you are from the first day of your last period. Adjusts for your cycle length, with the full 40-week breakdown.
h2: How the due date is calculated
Why a dating scan replaces this estimate
When to contact a doctor or midwife

schemaFaqs.question: How accurate is a due date calculator?
schemaFaqs.answer: The arithmetic is exact; the assumptions behind it are not. Only about one pregnancy in twenty ends on its estimated date, and the great majority of births happen in the weeks either side of it. A first-trimester scan is the accurate version, and once you have had one, its date is the one that is used.

schemaFaqs.question: How many weeks pregnant am I?
schemaFaqs.answer: Pregnancy is counted from the first day of your last period, not from conception — which is why you are already around four weeks pregnant when a test first turns positive. Conception happens roughly two weeks after that first day, so the pregnancy is always dated about two weeks 'older' than the embryo.

schemaFaqs.question: What does 9w 3d mean?
schemaFaqs.answer: Nine completed weeks and three days since the first day of your last period. Maternity records are written this way because a whole week is too coarse when a scan or a test has to happen inside a particular window.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use this if my cycles are irregular?
schemaFaqs.answer: You can, and entering your usual cycle length will get you closer than the 28-day default. But an irregular cycle is exactly the case where the last period is a weak anchor, so treat the result as a rough guide until you have been scanned.

schemaFaqs.question: Does the due date change after a scan?
schemaFaqs.answer: Often, yes — usually by a few days. The scan measures the baby instead of counting from a remembered date, so it is the one that is kept. A change of a week or more is common when the date of the last period was uncertain.

faqs.question: How accurate is a due date calculator?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic is exact; the assumptions behind it are not. Only about one pregnancy in twenty ends on its estimated date, and the great majority of births happen in the weeks either side of it. A first-trimester scan is the accurate version, and once you have had one, its date is the one that is used.

faqs.question: How many weeks pregnant am I?
faqs.answer: Pregnancy is counted from the first day of your last period, not from conception — which is why you are already around four weeks pregnant when a test first turns positive. Conception happens roughly two weeks after that first day, so the pregnancy is always dated about two weeks 'older' than the embryo.

faqs.question: What does 9w 3d mean?
faqs.answer: Nine completed weeks and three days since the first day of your last period. Maternity records are written this way because a whole week is too coarse when a scan or a test has to happen inside a particular window.

faqs.answer: You can, and entering your usual cycle length will get you closer than the 28-day default. But an irregular cycle is exactly the case where the last period is a weak anchor, so treat the result as a rough guide until you have been scanned.

title: Osteoporosis Risk Checker Spain | Should You Get a Bone Density Scan?
description: Check the published risk factors for osteoporosis and fragility fracture, and see whether guidelines recommend you be assessed. Not FRAX, not a diagnosis — a case-finding checklist you can bring to a doctor.
h2: Risk factors for a fragility fracture
Who guidelines say should be assessed
What this checker cannot tell you
Want to talk about your bone health?

schemaFaqs.question: Is this the same as FRAX?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. FRAX is a separate, proprietary tool developed by the University of Sheffield, and its coefficients are not published — this tool does not reproduce it or claim to match its output. This is a case-finding checklist based on published guidance (NICE CG146): it tells you whether it's worth being assessed, never a fracture probability.

schemaFaqs.question: What is a DXA scan?
schemaFaqs.answer: A dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scan — a low-dose X-ray that measures bone density, usually at the hip and spine. It is the test an assessment actually relies on; nothing on this page replaces it.

schemaFaqs.question: Does having risk factors mean I have osteoporosis?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. A flagged risk factor means guidelines recommend you be assessed, not that you have the condition. Many people with risk factors have a normal bone density scan, and osteoporosis can also occur with none of the factors listed here.

schemaFaqs.question: What if my result is 'no specific risk factors flagged' but I'm still concerned?
schemaFaqs.answer: Raise it with a doctor anyway. This tool covers the risk factors named in one clinical guideline; it does not cover every personal or family history that might be relevant, and a conversation costs nothing this checklist can weigh.

schemaFaqs.question: Who actually diagnoses osteoporosis?
schemaFaqs.answer: A doctor, from a DXA bone density scan — usually a T-score of -2.5 or below at the hip or spine. A risk-factor questionnaire like this one can only suggest who should have that scan; it cannot diagnose anything itself.

schemaFaqs.question: Does this checker store my answers?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The scoring runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you select is sent to our servers or saved.

schemaFaqs.question: Does the Spanish health system offer DXA bone density scans?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. DXA scanning is available through the public health system on referral, and privately without one in most clinics. Spain follows a risk-factor-led approach similar to this checker's — risk factors decide who is assessed, not age or a scan alone.

schemaFaqs.question: Where can I get assessed for osteoporosis in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Start with a medical appointment. The doctor will go through your risk factors and, where the guideline threshold is met, refer you for a DXA scan through the public system or arrange a private one.

title: Ovulation Calculator Spain | Fertile Window Dates
description: Work out your fertile window and estimated ovulation day from the first day of your last period. Adjusts for your own cycle length, with the six most fertile days set out day by day.
h2: When to talk to a doctor

schemaFaqs.question: When am I most fertile?
schemaFaqs.answer: On the day of ovulation and the two days before it. The window as a whole covers about six days: the five before ovulation plus the day itself. Sperm survive up to five days and the egg under one, which is why the window opens early and closes fast.

schemaFaqs.question: Does ovulation always happen on day 14?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. Day 14 is only true of a textbook 28-day cycle. Ovulation sits roughly 14 days before your next period, so on a 32-day cycle it lands around day 18 and on a 24-day cycle around day 10. Counting 14 days forward from your last period is the commonest way to get the timing wrong.

schemaFaqs.question: How do I work out ovulation with irregular cycles?
schemaFaqs.answer: Enter your usual cycle length and treat the result as a wide estimate rather than a date. If your cycles vary by more than a few days, ovulation predictor kits or tracking cervical mucus will tell you far more than any calendar calculation, and cycles that are consistently under 21 or over 35 days are worth a doctor's opinion.

schemaFaqs.question: Can I use an ovulation calculator as contraception?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. It is not a contraceptive method and should never be used as one. Ovulation shifts between cycles, sperm can survive up to five days, and pregnancy is possible on days this calculator marks as outside the fertile window. If you are avoiding pregnancy, use a recognised method of contraception.

schemaFaqs.question: When can I take a pregnancy test after ovulation?
schemaFaqs.answer: Most home tests are reliable from the day your period is due, which is about 14 days after ovulation — the "test from" date in the read-out. Testing earlier can give a negative result even when you are pregnant, because there is not yet enough hCG in urine to detect.

schemaFaqs.question: Does this ovulation calculator store my details?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The calculation runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to our servers or saved.

schemaFaqs.question: Where do I get fertility advice in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Through your local health centre: the family doctor makes the first assessment of both partners and orders the initial blood tests, referring on to gynaecology or a reproductive unit when that is the next step. Our registered doctors can review irregular cycles and preconception checks by video in the meantime.

schemaFaqs.question: Where can I buy ovulation tests in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: In pharmacies and parapharmacies, without a prescription. They detect the LH surge in urine 24 to 36 hours before the egg is released, so start testing a few days before the date estimated above.

title: Tonsillitis or Strep Throat? Checker Spain · Global Health
description: Answer five questions about your sore throat and see how likely a bacterial cause is, using the McIsaac score clinicians use. Includes the warning signs that need urgent care. Not a diagnosis and not a strep test.
h1: Tonsillitis and strep throat checker Spain
h2: The five things the score asks about
What this checker cannot tell you
When a sore throat needs urgent care
Need someone to look at your throat?

schemaFaqs.question: Is this the same as a strep test?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. A strep test is a swab of the throat, either sent to a laboratory or run as a rapid antigen test in the clinic. This page estimates how likely a bacterial cause is from your symptoms, which is what a clinician uses to decide whether that swab is worth taking. It cannot replace the swab.

schemaFaqs.question: What is the difference between tonsillitis and strep throat?
schemaFaqs.answer: Tonsillitis describes inflamed tonsils, whatever the cause — most often a virus. Strep throat is tonsillitis or pharyngitis caused by one particular bacterium, Streptococcus pyogenes, known as group A strep. Every case of strep throat is tonsillitis; most tonsillitis is not strep throat.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need antibiotics for a sore throat?
schemaFaqs.answer: That is a decision for a doctor, not for this page. Most sore throats are viral, where antibiotics do nothing and still carry side effects. A high score means the odds of a bacterial cause are high enough that a doctor would usually examine you and consider testing — it does not mean antibiotics are indicated.

schemaFaqs.question: How long should a sore throat last?
schemaFaqs.answer: Most settle within about a week, whether viral or bacterial. A sore throat that is still worsening after a week, or that comes with a fever you cannot bring down, is worth having looked at regardless of what this checker says.

schemaFaqs.question: Why does the score subtract a point if I am over 45?
schemaFaqs.answer: Because strep throat becomes uncommon with age. The original Centor score was built for adults and over-called bacterial infection in older patients; McIsaac's age adjustment corrects for that in both directions, adding a point for children aged 3 to 14, where strep is most common.

schemaFaqs.question: Does this checker store my answers?
schemaFaqs.answer: No. The scoring runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you select is sent to our servers or saved.

schemaFaqs.question: Do I need a prescription for antibiotics in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: Yes. Antibiotics are prescription-only in Spain, so a pharmacy cannot dispense them for a sore throat without one. A pharmacist can advise on pain relief and tell you whether they think you should be seen, but the prescribing decision belongs to a doctor who has examined you.

schemaFaqs.question: Where can I get a sore throat examined in Spain?
schemaFaqs.answer: A family doctor can look at your throat and take a throat swab if the pattern warrants it. Emergency departments are for the warning signs listed above, not for ordinary tonsillitis. Our registered doctors can review your symptoms by video consultation and advise whether a swab or an in-person examination is the right next step.

It takes about a minute.Uses the published McIsaac score, age-adjusted — not a score we inventedFlags the warning signs that need urgent care before it scores anythingRuns in your browser — nothing is sent or storedYour symptomsAgeyearsFever during this illnessYesNoA temperature over 38 °C, or feeling feverish and shivery, at any point since it started.Do you have a cough?YesNoA cough points towards a virus, so the score counts its absence rather than its presence.Tender, swollen glands in the front of the neckYesNoJust under the jaw on either side, sore when you press them — not the glands at the back of the neck.White patches or swelling on the tonsilsYesNoLook with a torch at the back of the throat. This is hard to judge on yourself and is the weakest answer in the score.Trouble breathing, swallowing your own saliva, or opening your mouthYesNoAlso drooling, a muffled voice, severe pain on one side only, or a stiff or swollen neck.A rash along with the sore throatYesNoOften a fine, rough, sandpaper-like rash on the chest or neck.A condition or medicine that weakens your immune systemYesNoIncluding chemotherapy, carbimazole, methotrexate or long-term steroids. A sore throat can be the first sign of a problem with your white blood cells.1pointsBacterial infection unlikelyThis pattern is still much more often viral than bacterial. Self-care is usually right, but this is not a negative test — see a doctor if the pain worsens, a fever climbs, or you are no better after a week.Symptoms matched1 / 4Age adjustment0This estimates how likely a sore throat is to be bacterial. It is not a strep test and not a diagnosis — only a throat swab or an examination can confirm one. A low score means a bacterial infection is unlikely, not that it has been ruled out. Never start or stop antibiotics based on this page.01What your score meansThe score runs from -1 to 5. Four features each add a point — a fever, no cough, tender glands at the front of the neck, and white patches on the tonsils — and age adjusts the total up or down. Children aged 3 to 14 gain a point; adults over 45 lose one, because strep throat becomes uncommon with age.The bands below describe how likely a bacterial cause is, not how bad the sore throat feels. A viral sore throat can hurt a great deal and still score zero.0 or belowBacterial causeVery unlikelyWhat it usually meansSelf-care. Rest, fluids and pain relief; see a doctor if it is no better after a week.1Bacterial causeUnlikelyWhat it usually meansUsually self-care, with a review if it worsens rather than settles.2Bacterial causePossibleWhat it usually meansThe point at which a doctor would normally want to look at your throat rather than guess.3Bacterial causeMore likelyWhat it usually meansGuidelines prompt an examination and often a swab. Arrange a consultation.4 or 5Bacterial causeMost likelyWhat it usually meansThe group most likely to be tested and to be considered for antibiotics. Arrange to be seen.What each score band usually meansScoreBacterial causeWhat it usually means0 or belowVery unlikelySelf-care. Rest, fluids and pain relief; see a doctor if it is no better after a week.1UnlikelyUsually self-care, with a review if it worsens rather than settles.2PossibleThe point at which a doctor would normally want to look at your throat rather than guess.3More likelyGuidelines prompt an examination and often a swab. Arrange a consultation.4 or 5Most likelyThe group most likely to be tested and to be considered for antibiotics. Arrange to be seen.Based on the McIsaac (age-adjusted Centor) score, the rule NICE guideline NG84 accepts for assessing a sore throat. Bands are shown as likelihoods rather than percentages on purpose: the published percentages come from clinicians examining a throat, and answers you give about your own throat are not the same measurement.02The five things the score asks aboutEach one is there because it shifts the odds between a virus and a bacterial infection, and together they do better than any single symptom on its own.Fever — bacterial throat infections are more likely than viral ones to come with a temperature over 38 °C.No cough — a cough points strongly towards a virus, so the score counts its absence. This is the criterion people most often get backwards.Tender, swollen glands at the front of the neck — the lymph nodes that drain the tonsils, which swell and hurt when the tonsils are infected.White patches or swelling on the tonsils — pus on the tonsils raises the odds of a bacterial cause, although a virus can produce it too.Age — strep throat peaks between 5 and 15 and becomes uncommon after 45, so the score adds a point for children and subtracts one for older adults.03What this checker cannot tell youA score sorts likelihoods. It does not identify what is growing in your throat, and it was designed for a clinician who is looking at one.It is not a strep test. Only a throat swab or a rapid antigen test can confirm a bacterial cause, and a doctor takes it.A low score is not a negative result. It means a bacterial cause is unlikely on the balance of odds, not that it has been ruled out.Two of the answers are examination findings. A clinician feels the glands and looks at the tonsils with a light; judging those on yourself is the least reliable part of this page.It does not decide anything about antibiotics. That is a prescribing decision a doctor makes after examining you, weighing your history and often a swab result.It says nothing about glandular fever, which can look identical at first and is common in teenagers and young adults whose sore throat drags on.It does not apply to children under 3, where it is not reliable and a doctor should assess instead.04When a sore throat needs urgent careThese override the score completely. schemaFaqs.question: ¿Cómo funciona una consulta online?
schemaFaqs.answer: Reserve una cita online, elija un horario disponible y únase a su consulta por videollamada segura desde su teléfono u ordenador. Su médico revisará sus síntomas e historial y le aconsejará los siguientes pasos.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Quiénes son los médicos?
schemaFaqs.answer: Todos los médicos de Global Health son colegiados a través de Organización Médica Colegial (colegios de médicos). Los datos de colegiación se muestran en el perfil de cada médico.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Qué idiomas están disponibles?
schemaFaqs.answer: Las consultas están disponibles en varios idiomas, según disponibilidad del médico. Puede elegir médico por idioma al reservar.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Es segura una consulta online?
schemaFaqs.answer: Sí. Todas las consultas se realizan mediante videollamada segura conforme a los estándares nacionales de telemedicina, y su información clínica se trata de forma confidencial.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Cómo reservo una cita?
schemaFaqs.answer: Elija un servicio, seleccione un horario disponible y complete su reserva online. Recibirá confirmación por correo electrónico antes de la cita.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Cuánto cuesta una consulta?
schemaFaqs.answer: Las consultas en Global Health cuestan desde 29,00 €. Sin costes ocultos ni suscripción obligatoria.

María Fernanda Ocampo Mora es médica con amplia experiencia en medicina de urgencias, medicina general y familiar, y medicina estética, una clínica que combina la solidez de quien ha trabajado en hospitales de alta complejidad con la sensibilidad estética y la precisión de quien ha formado a nivel de maestría en medicina estética avanzada. Se graduó como médica en la Universidad Libre de Cali y ha desarrollado su carrera en entornos hospitalarios de alto nivel en España y Colombia. En España ha trabajado en el Hospital Quirón Málaga y el Hospital Quirón Marbella, dos de los centros hospitalarios privados de mayor prestigio del país, proporcionando atención médica urgente, diagnóstico rápido y atención multidisciplinar en situaciones críticas. En Colombia acumuló años de experiencia en unidades de cuidados intensivos (UCI) y servicios de urgencias, atendiendo pacientes críticos y casos médicos complejos. Paralelamente a su práctica hospitalaria, la Dra. Ocampo ha desarrollado una trayectoria sólida en medicina estética, con un Máster en Medicina Estética y un Máster en Tratamientos Faciales con formación académica europea certificada. Actualmente ejerce en Clínica IOX Marbella y Clínica Vasari, donde combina procedimientos mínimamente invasivos, tratamientos faciales y corporales y protocolos de tratamiento personalizados con los más altos estándares de seguridad médica. Su formación en urgencias y UCI le proporciona un criterio clínico de alta fiabilidad, la capacidad de evaluar rápidamente si un síntoma es banal o requiere atención inmediata, que es especialmente valiosa en una consulta online donde la toma de decisiones en tiempo real marca la diferencia. title: Baja laboral por ansiedad: quién la emite en España
description: Baja laboral por ansiedad en España: quién emite el parte de baja, qué evalúa el médico, qué información recibe la empresa y qué es la inspección médica.
h1: Baja laboral por ansiedad: quién la emite y qué se evalúa
h2: Qué es exactamente una baja por ansiedad
Quién emite el parte de baja y por qué importa
Qué ocurre en la consulta y cómo llegar preparado
Qué sabe la empresa y qué es la inspección médica
Qué puede y qué no puede una consulta privada online
Qué se hace durante la baja, y la vuelta al trabajo
Cuándo esto deja de ser un asunto de papeles

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Quién puede darme la baja por ansiedad en España?
schemaFaqs.answer: El parte de baja lo emite el médico de atención primaria del Servicio Público de Salud cuando el proceso es contingencia común, o el médico de la mutua cuando corresponde a contingencia profesional. Una consulta privada puede evaluarle, tratarle y emitir un justificante médico de ausencia, pero no emite el parte de baja.

schemaFaqs.question: Mi médico no me da la baja por ansiedad, ¿qué puedo hacer?
schemaFaqs.answer: Vuelva a consultar describiendo el impacto funcional en términos concretos: qué tareas de su puesto ha dejado de poder hacer, cuánto duerme, qué errores ha cometido, qué síntomas físicos tiene y con qué frecuencia. Puede pedir una nueva valoración. Una segunda opinión privada no emite el parte, pero ayuda a documentar la evolución.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Mi empresa puede saber que estoy de baja por ansiedad?
schemaFaqs.answer: Su empresa conoce la existencia de la baja y su duración estimada, no el diagnóstico. Los datos de salud están especialmente protegidos por la normativa de protección de datos. Contarlo es una decisión suya, nunca una obligación.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Qué pasa si me llama la inspección médica estando de baja?
schemaFaqs.answer: Es un control ordinario del proceso, no una acusación. Acuda a la cita, lleve informes y documentación clínica y describa su estado y su evolución con concreción. La incomparecencia sin justificar tiene consecuencias sobre la prestación.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Se puede viajar o salir de casa estando de baja?
schemaFaqs.answer: Estar de baja no implica permanecer en casa, y en muchos cuadros de ansiedad la actividad forma parte del tratamiento. Lo que no procede son actividades incompatibles con la recuperación o que contradigan la incapacidad. Antes de un desplazamiento, especialmente al extranjero, consúltelo con su médico y con la Seguridad Social.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Cuánto dura una baja por ansiedad?
schemaFaqs.answer: No hay una duración fija: depende de la gravedad, de la respuesta al tratamiento y del puesto de trabajo. Los límites máximos y las prórrogas están fijados por ley y cambian, así que conviene confirmarlos en la Seguridad Social y no en un artículo.

faqs.question: ¿Quién puede darme la baja por ansiedad en España?
faqs.answer: El parte de baja lo emite el médico de atención primaria del Servicio Público de Salud cuando el proceso es contingencia común, o el médico de la mutua cuando corresponde a contingencia profesional. Una consulta privada puede evaluarle, tratarle y emitir un justificante médico de ausencia, pero no emite el parte de baja.

faqs.question: Mi médico no me da la baja por ansiedad, ¿qué puedo hacer?
faqs.answer: Vuelva a consultar describiendo el impacto funcional en términos concretos: qué tareas de su puesto ha dejado de poder hacer, cuánto duerme, qué errores ha cometido, qué síntomas físicos tiene y con qué frecuencia. Puede pedir una nueva valoración. Una segunda opinión privada no emite el parte, pero ayuda a documentar la evolución.

faqs.question: ¿Mi empresa puede saber que estoy de baja por ansiedad?
faqs.answer: Su empresa conoce la existencia de la baja y su duración estimada, no el diagnóstico. Los datos de salud están especialmente protegidos por la normativa de protección de datos. Contarlo es una decisión suya, nunca una obligación.

faqs.question: ¿Qué pasa si me llama la inspección médica estando de baja?
faqs.answer: Es un control ordinario del proceso, no una acusación. Acuda a la cita, lleve informes y documentación clínica y describa su estado y su evolución con concreción. La incomparecencia sin justificar tiene consecuencias sobre la prestación.

faqs.question: ¿Se puede viajar o salir de casa estando de baja?
faqs.answer: Estar de baja no implica permanecer en casa, y en muchos cuadros de ansiedad la actividad forma parte del tratamiento. Lo que no procede son actividades incompatibles con la recuperación o que contradigan la incapacidad. Antes de un desplazamiento, especialmente al extranjero, consúltelo con su médico y con la Seguridad Social.

body: Todos los artículosSalud MentalBaja laboral por ansiedad: quién la emite y qué se evalúaLa baja por ansiedad es una incapacidad temporal y la emite el médico del sistema público o de la mutua, no una consulta privada. Explicamos qué evalúa el médico, qué sabe la empresa, qué es la inspección médica y qué puede hacer por usted una consulta online.Global Health Medical Team14 de agosto de 202613 min de lecturaRevisado clínicamente por Dr. Eduardo Daniel Rodríguez OlivasEspaña · Guía para trabajadoresNi es un capricho ni se concede por pedirla. Es una decisión clínica sobre si usted está, en este momento, en condiciones de trabajar.Una baja laboral por ansiedad es una incapacidad temporal como cualquier otra: el médico certifica que un problema de salud le impide trabajar durante un tiempo. En España el parte de baja lo emite el médico del Servicio Público de Salud o, cuando la contingencia corresponde a la mutua, el médico de la mutua. Una consulta privada —también la nuestra— no emite el parte de baja: puede evaluarle, tratarle, emitir un justificante médico de ausencia e informar el proceso, que no es lo mismo. Lo que decide la baja no es la palabra «ansiedad», sino el grado de afectación funcional que el médico observa en la consulta.La emite el SNS o la mutuaLa empresa no recibe el diagnósticoLo que se evalúa es la funciónConsulta de salud mentalIncapacidad temporal — Seguridad SocialQué cubre esta guíaQuién puede emitir el parte de baja y por qué la vía privada no es esa vía.Qué evalúa realmente el médico cuando alguien consulta por ansiedad, y cómo llegar preparado a esa consulta.Qué información recibe la empresa, qué es la inspección médica y qué puede preguntarle.La duración máxima, los días de espera, el porcentaje de la base reguladora y los días cotizados exigidos son materia legal y cambian. Aquí no se citan cifras: cada punto remite a la Seguridad Social.GHGlobal Health Medical TeamRevisado por el equipo médico de Global Health.Punto de partidaQué es exactamente una baja por ansiedadNo existe una «baja por ansiedad» como categoría aparte. Existe una incapacidad temporal cuya causa es un trastorno de ansiedad.Esa distinción no es un tecnicismo. Significa que el criterio es el mismo que en una lumbalgia o en una neumonía: ¿le impide este problema de salud desempeñar su trabajo ahora mismo? No se evalúa cuánto sufre en abstracto, ni si su malestar está justificado, ni si su empresa se porta bien con usted. Se evalúa función.Por eso dos personas con el mismo diagnóstico pueden recibir respuestas distintas. Una crisis puntual en alguien que sigue durmiendo y desempeñando sus tareas no es lo mismo que un cuadro con insomnio mantenido, incapacidad de concentración y deterioro claro del rendimiento.Síntomas — ansiedad anticipatoria, crisis, insomnio, síntomas somáticos, irritabilidad, evitación.Función — concentración, memoria de trabajo, tolerancia al estrés, capacidad de conducir o de manejar maquinaria, trato con público.Riesgo — ideación autolítica, consumo de alcohol o de otras sustancias, seguridad propia y de terceros en el puesto.Contexto — qué hace exactamente en su trabajo, porque la misma clínica incapacita para un puesto y no para otro.Evolución — desde cuándo, qué ha probado, qué ha empeorado o mejorado.Ansiedad no significa «no es real»Los síntomas físicos de la ansiedad —taquicardia, opresión torácica, falta de aire, mareo, molestias digestivas— son síntomas auténticos, no imaginados. Y a la inversa: precisamente porque se parecen a los de otras enfermedades, un cuadro nuevo merece ser evaluado y no atribuido a los nervios sin más.CircuitoQuién emite el parte de baja y por qué importaEsta es la pregunta que más tiempo hace perder, porque la respuesta depende de la contingencia.Si el proceso se considera contingencia común, el parte de baja lo emite su médico de atención primaria del Servicio Público de Salud. Si se considera contingencia profesional —accidente de trabajo o enfermedad profesional—, corresponde a la mutua colaboradora con la Seguridad Social. En ambos casos hay partes de confirmación periódicos y un parte de alta, y en ambos casos el seguimiento del proceso no lo lleva una consulta privada.El parte de baja es un documento del sistema público o de la mutua, no un certificado privado.La prestación económica depende de la Seguridad Social y de sus requisitos, no del médico que le atiende.El INSS y la mutua pueden citarle para revisión a lo largo del proceso.Si no está de acuerdo con un alta, existen vías de reclamación: la Seguridad Social explica cuáles y en qué plazos.Conviene decir con claridad algo que se olvida a menudo: solicitar una baja no es una acusación contra su empresa, ni requiere que su empresa esté de acuerdo. Es una decisión clínica.Requisitos, plazos y reclamaciones: Seguridad Social.PreparaciónQué ocurre en la consulta y cómo llegar preparadoLa queja más repetida —«mi médico no me da la baja»— casi nunca se resuelve insistiendo, y casi siempre se resuelve explicando mejor.El médico dispone de pocos minutos y de lo que usted le cuente. Si describe su estado en términos generales —«estoy fatal», «no puedo más»—, está pidiéndole que adivine el impacto funcional. Si lo describe en términos concretos, le está dando exactamente el material sobre el que se decide una incapacidad temporal.Qué ha dejado de poder hacer: tareas concretas de su puesto que antes hacía y ahora no.Sueño: cuántas noches, cuántas horas, si se despierta de madrugada.Errores y olvidos en el trabajo, y si ha habido alguna situación de riesgo.Síntomas físicos y su frecuencia: crisis, taquicardia, mareo, molestias digestivas.Riesgo: si ha tenido ideas de hacerse daño, dígalo. Es la información que más cambia la conducta clínica y la que más se calla.Si la valoración no refleja su situación, tiene derecho a pedir una nueva y a explicar lo que faltó. Una segunda opinión privada no emite el parte de baja, pero ayuda a ordenar los hechos clínicos y a documentar la evolución.Sus derechosQué sabe la empresa y qué es la inspección médicaLa confusión aquí es enorme, y produce miedo innecesario en gente que está ya suficientemente mal.Su empresa no recibe su diagnóstico. Lo que se comunica es la existencia de la baja y su duración estimada. Los datos de salud son una categoría especialmente protegida por la normativa de protección de datos, y ni el departamento de personal ni su jefe tienen derecho a que se les diga qué le ocurre. Puede contarlo si quiere, pero es una decisión suya, no una obligación.La inspección médica —una citación del INSS o de la mutua— tampoco es un castigo ni una acusación. Es un control del proceso, y forma parte del funcionamiento normal de la incapacidad temporal. Le citan, le valoran, y esa valoración puede confirmar la baja o proponer el alta.Acuda a la cita: la incomparecencia sin justificar tiene consecuencias sobre la prestación.Lleve informes, recetas y cualquier documentación clínica del proceso.Responda a lo que le pregunten sobre su estado y su evolución, con la misma concreción que en la consulta.No tiene que demostrar que sufre. Tiene que describir cómo está y qué puede y qué no puede hacer.Sobre viajar o salir de casa estando de bajaEstar de baja no equivale a arresto domiciliario, y en muchos cuadros de ansiedad salir a caminar forma parte del tratamiento. Lo que no procede es realizar actividades incompatibles con la recuperación o que contradigan la incapacidad alegada. Si va a desplazarse, especialmente al extranjero, consulte antes con su médico y con la Seguridad Social: las consecuencias de hacerlo mal afectan a la prestación, no solo a su salud.Protección de datos de salud: AEPD. Control de la incapacidad temporal: Seguridad Social.TransparenciaQué puede y qué no puede una consulta privada onlineLo decimos primero y sin rodeos, porque es la pregunta con la que llega la mayoría de la gente.Una consulta privada, presencial o por vídeo, no emite el parte de baja de incapacidad temporal. Ese documento pertenece al circuito del Servicio Público de Salud o de la mutua. Cualquier servicio que le prometa «la baja» por internet le está prometiendo algo que no está en su mano, y conviene desconfiar de esa promesa antes de pagarla.Lo que sí puede hacer una consulta privada es, con frecuencia, lo que la persona necesita esa misma semana:Evaluarle sin lista de espera y decirle con franqueza qué está viendo.Emitir un justificante médico de la ausencia, que no es un parte de baja y que así se lo diremos.Iniciar tratamiento cuando está indicado, y explicarle qué esperar y en cuánto tiempo.Descartar otras causas de síntomas que se parecen a la ansiedad y no lo son.Ordenar el caso para su médico de atención primaria: qué contar, qué documentar, qué pedir.Acompañar la vuelta al trabajo, que es la fase que casi nadie prepara.Puede comprobar la colegiación de cualquier médico en el registro público del CGCOM, con nosotros igual que con cualquier otro.Ninguna consulta garantiza una bajaUn médico que garantice el resultado antes de evaluarle no está ejerciendo la medicina. La decisión depende de lo que muestre la valoración clínica, y en el caso de la incapacidad temporal depende además de un circuito en el que la medicina privada no participa.Durante la bajaQué se hace durante la baja, y la vuelta al trabajoUna baja por ansiedad sin tratamiento suele ser una baja que se repite.El tiempo, por sí solo, rara vez resuelve un trastorno de ansiedad. Lo que lo resuelve se decide caso a caso: psicoterapia, medicación cuando está indicada, intervención sobre el sueño, actividad física, reducción del alcohol y —cuando la causa está ahí— cambios en las condiciones de trabajo.La vuelta merece prepararse con la misma seriedad que la salida. Reincorporarse el lunes al mismo puesto, con la misma carga y sin haber cambiado nada, es la receta habitual de la recaída. Hable con antelación de la reincorporación con su médico y, si su empresa dispone de vigilancia de la salud, con el servicio de prevención: la adaptación del puesto es una vía formal y existe precisamente para esto.Mantenga horarios de sueño estables, aunque no trabaje.No abandone el tratamiento en cuanto mejore: la mejoría inicial no es el final del proceso.SeguridadCuándo esto deja de ser un asunto de papelesHay situaciones en las que la baja es lo de menos y la atención es inmediata.Ideas de quitarse la vida, un plan, o la sensación de no poder garantizar su propia seguridad.Incapacidad de cuidar de sí mismo o de personas a su cargo.Consumo de alcohol o de otras sustancias para poder funcionar o para dormir.Dolor torácico intenso, falta de aire en reposo o desmayo — que pueden parecer ansiedad y no serlo.En España existe la línea 024 de atención a la conducta suicida, disponible las veinticuatro horas y gratuita. Ante una emergencia médica, llame al 112. title: Cómo bajar la tensión alta: qué funciona de verdad
description: Cinco medidas con efecto medido sobre la tensión, si se puede bajar rápido, qué dice la guía ESC 2024 sobre infusiones y remedios, y cuándo llamar al 112.
h1: Cómo bajar la tensión: lo que funciona según las guías y lo que solo parece funcionar

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Cómo bajar la tensión alta rápidamente en casa?
schemaFaqs.answer: No hay un método rápido con evidencia. Siéntese, repose cinco minutos y vuelva a medir. Si sigue en 180/110 o más con síntomas, llame al 112; sin síntomas, pida valoración médica el mismo día.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿La tila o la manzanilla bajan la tensión?
schemaFaqs.answer: Pueden relajar y cambiar la lectura del momento. No tratan la hipertensión y ninguna guía las recomienda con ese fin.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Las pastillas de la tensión son para siempre?
schemaFaqs.answer: A menudo sí, pero no siempre. La guía ESC 2024 reconoce que los cambios de estilo de vida pueden permitir reducir o retirar fármacos. Es una decisión médica, nunca por su cuenta.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Cuánto tardan en notarse los cambios de estilo de vida?
schemaFaqs.answer: Semanas, no días. La guía europea de 2024 da tres meses de estilo de vida antes de reevaluar si hace falta medicación.

Sí hay cinco medidas que la bajan en unas semanas, y una lista corta de remedios que no hacen nada.Para bajar la tensión de forma duradera hay cinco medidas con efecto medido: reducir la sal a menos de 5 gramos al día, hacer al menos 150 minutos semanales de ejercicio aeróbico moderado, perder peso si sobra, limitar el alcohol y seguir una dieta tipo mediterránea o DASH rica en potasio. La guía europea de 2024 da tres meses de estilo de vida antes de decidir sobre fármacos si la tensión está elevada sin ser hipertensión. Ninguna infusión ni remedio casero la baja de forma rápida y demostrada. Con 180/110 y síntomas, 112.Sal por debajo de 5 g al día (unos 2 g de sodio)150 minutos semanales de ejercicio: unos 7 mmHg menos de sistólicaTres meses de estilo de vida antes de decidir sobre fármacos, si no hay riesgo altoGuía ESC 2024 de hipertensiónSíntomas de tensión alta y urgenciasAntes de cambiar nadaMida bien. Siete días, mañana y tarde, sentado y tras cinco minutos de reposo. Una lectura aislada no decide nada.Si ya toma pastillas, no las cambie ni las deje por su cuenta. Aquí la guía recomienda tres meses de medidas de estilo de vida antes de valorar fármacos, salvo riesgo cardiovascular alto.Hipertensión: 140/90 o más, confirmada fuera de la consulta. En casa, el umbral es 135/85.El objetivo en tratamiento es una sistólica de 120 a 129 mmHg si se tolera, más laxo a partir de los 85 años o con fragilidad. Lo que cambia entre ellas es cuánto bajan y cuánto tardan.1. Sal por debajo de 5 g al día (unos 2 g de sodio). El pan, los embutidos, el queso y los precocinados aportan más que el salero.2. Ejercicio aeróbico, 150 minutos semanales. La revisión de la guía ESC 2024 publicada en PMC cifra la bajada media en 7,2 mmHg de sistólica y 5,6 de diastólica. Añada ejercicio de fuerza dos o tres días por semana.3. Peso. IMC entre 20 y 25, cintura por debajo de 94 cm en hombres y 80 en mujeres. La guía estadounidense ACC/AHA estima alrededor de 1 mmHg menos por cada kilo perdido.4. Alcohol. Límite ESC de 100 g de alcohol a la semana; la guía ESH 2023 recomienda acercarse a la abstinencia.5. Dieta mediterránea o DASH, con potasio. La ESC recomienda aumentar el potasio de la dieta, por encima de 3,5 g al día, si el riñón funciona bien.Dejar de fumar está en la misma lista por otro motivo: apenas mueve el tensiómetro y sí reduce el riesgo de infarto e ictus, que es para lo que se baja la tensión.ESC 2024, revisión de la guía ESC 2024 (PMC) y OMS, ficha de hipertensión (2025).Semanas, no minutos¿Se puede bajar la tensión rápidamente?No de forma útil. Lo que baja la tensión en minutos es sentarse y descansar, y eso solo corrige la lectura, no la enfermedad.«Cómo bajar la tensión en cinco minutos» tiene respuesta corta: la respiración lenta relaja y puede restar unos puntos durante la medición, pero el metaanálisis del European Heart Journal de 2022 no encontró efecto significativo de la respiración guiada frente a la atención habitual, y la guía ESC 2024 no la recomienda. Las medidas reales tardan semanas. Por eso la guía ESC da tres meses de estilo de vida antes de revisar si hace falta medicación: con menos tiempo no se ve el efecto.European Heart Journal 2022, metaanálisis sobre respiración guiada.Tila, manzanilla y compañíaRemedios de la abuela para bajar la tensión: qué dice la evidenciaNinguna guía europea, ni la OMS, ni la Sociedad Española de Hipertensión recogen una infusión, un alimento o un truco que baje la tensión de forma aguda.Tila, manzanilla, valeriana: pueden relajar. Relajarse baja la lectura del momento. No tratan la hipertensión.Ajo, limón, vinagre: aparecen en las webs de cardiología solo como sustitutos de la sal. Ese es todo su papel.«Pastillas para la tensión sin receta»: no existen. Cualquier producto que se venda así es un suplemento sin efecto demostrado.Tomar una pastilla extra cuando la tensión sube: la SEH-LELHA lo dice sin rodeos: nunca tome decisiones por su cuenta. Una bajada brusca puede ser peor que la subida.Cuándo dejar la infusión y llamar al 112Con 180/110 o más y dolor en el pecho, dificultad para respirar, debilidad en un lado del cuerpo, dificultad para hablar o confusión, es una emergencia. Con 180/110 sin síntomas no lo es, pero necesita valoración médica el mismo día, no una tila. Los detalles están en nuestra guía de síntomas de tensión alta y urgencias.SEH-LELHA, automedición de la presión arterial.AMPACómo saber si está funcionandoCon un tensiómetro de brazo validado y un protocolo de siete días. Una lectura suelta no sirve para decidir nada.SEH-LELHA y ESC coinciden: siete días, dos o tres lecturas por la mañana antes de la medicación y otras tantas por la tarde, sentado, espalda apoyada, brazo a la altura del corazón, cinco minutos de reposo. Se descarta el primer día y se hace la media. 135/85 o más en casa es hipertensión. Si quiere un plan con seguimiento, o ya tiene hipertensión estable y necesita revisar tratamiento, puede hacerlo en una consulta de enfermedades crónicas online; para cifras difíciles de controlar, en cardiología. Ninguna consulta sustituye la medición correcta en casa.SEMES, automedida de la presión arterial.Global Health EspañaSeguimiento médicoEl estilo de vida lo pone usted. Si sigue en 180/110 o más con síntomas, llame al 112; sin síntomas, pida valoración médica el mismo día.¿La tila o la manzanilla bajan la tensión?Pueden relajar y cambiar la lectura del momento. No tratan la hipertensión y ninguna guía las recomienda con ese fin.¿Las pastillas de la tensión son para siempre?A menudo sí, pero no siempre. La guía ESC 2024 reconoce que los cambios de estilo de vida pueden permitir reducir o retirar fármacos. title: Dermatólogo online: qué resuelve y qué no · Global Health
description: Dermatólogo online en España: qué problemas de piel se resuelven por vídeo o fotografía, cuáles exigen consulta presencial y cómo hacer buenas fotos.
h1: Dermatólogo online: qué puede resolver y qué necesita ser presencial
h2: Lo que una consulta de dermatología online resuelve bien
Lo que una consulta online no puede hacer
Cómo hacer fotografías con las que se pueda trabajar
Lunares y manchas: cuándo hay que ir en persona

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Qué puede diagnosticar un dermatólogo online?
schemaFaqs.answer: Con una buena historia clínica e imágenes correctas se manejan bien el acné, la rosácea, la dermatitis atópica y de contacto, la psoriasis, la urticaria, las micosis, la onicomicosis y la caída del cabello, además del seguimiento de tratamientos en curso.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Sirve una consulta online para revisar un lunar?
schemaFaqs.answer: Sirve para decidir la urgencia, no para descartar con una foto normal: la valoración de lesiones pigmentadas se basa en la dermatoscopia, y una cámara de móvil sin adaptador no la sustituye. Con un adaptador dermatoscópico para móvil sí se obtiene una dermatoscopia real. Aun así, ante un lunar nuevo, que cambia, que sangra o distinto del resto, el diagnóstico se cierra en persona; la consulta online decide la urgencia y emite la derivación.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Un dermatólogo online puede recetarme?
schemaFaqs.answer: Sí, cuando la valoración lo indica. Un médico colegiado puede emitir receta electrónica tras la consulta. Lo que no puede es prescribir sin evaluar, ni comprometer un tratamiento concreto antes de ver el caso.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Cómo hago buenas fotos para la consulta?
schemaFaqs.answer: Con luz natural y sin flash, tres tomas —general, media y de cerca—, enfocando sobre la lesión, con una regla o moneda como referencia de tamaño, sin filtros ni retoques. Si el proceso evoluciona, repita el mismo encuadre para poder comparar.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Existe el dermatólogo online gratis en España?
schemaFaqs.answer: La vía sin coste para el paciente es el Sistema Nacional de Salud, a través del médico de atención primaria, que valora y deriva; muchas comunidades usan teledermatología entre primaria y el servicio hospitalario. Los chats y aplicaciones gratuitas de autodiagnóstico no son consultas médicas y no emiten receta.

schemaFaqs.question: ¿Es lo mismo que ir al dermatólogo presencialmente?
schemaFaqs.answer: Para los procesos inflamatorios y crónicos, el resultado es muy similar y el seguimiento suele ser mejor por poder repetirse con más frecuencia. Para lesiones pigmentadas, biopsias, crioterapia o cirugía, la consulta presencial es imprescindible.
